requirements.title: Repository layout: one workspace and its library crates

requirement_statement.text:
The GitHub repository `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST contain one Cargo workspace,
declared in the root `Cargo.toml`.

The workspace members MUST be exactly these library crates. Amended 2026-10-25 ([ADR-RUN-0012](architecture.md), [ADR-RUN-0013](architecture.md)): `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` and `sc-cron` are members. Amended 2026-11-11 (PRD-STO-3): `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` holds the atm-core SQLite writer that sits behind `Storage<T>`; the earlier rule that it is not a store the daemon opens and not a template dependency is withdrawn. The generated daemon may depend on `sc-cron` only through the optional `cron` feature fixed by [REQ-RUN-0301](requirements.md); feature-off generated builds do not link it.

| Member path | Crate name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/sc-config` | `sc-config` | JSON config files with environment overrides |
| `crates/sc-transport` | `sc-transport` | UDS/TCP listener and client connector |
| `crates/sc-command` | `sc-command` | response envelope, `OpError`, REST and MCP conversions |
| `crates/sc-runtime` | `sc-runtime` | daemon assembly: `Daemon::builder()`, `daemon.lock`, `DaemonFixture` |
| `crates/sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | rusqlite write actor; one connection, one thread |
| `crates/sc-cron` | `sc-cron` | SQLite-backed cron; the app registers the job |
| `crates/sc-cron-commands` (Phase C target) | `sc-cron-commands` | optional standard cron DTOs and scheduler adapter; ADR-RUN-0019 |

Phase C amendment: the new adapter member is planned, not yet implemented.
Its default DTO graph and optional scheduler edge are defined by
REQ-RUN-0332 and NFR-CRNC-0001; no reverse core command/runtime edge is allowed.

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `template/` | the `cargo-generate` template root, including `template/cargo-generate.toml`, `template/AGENTS.md.j2` and `template/CLAUDE.md.j2` |
| `wizard/` | `wizard.json`, `answers.schema.json` (the options contract), `pages/` (wizard HTML pages), `fixtures/` (one answers JSON file per tested variant) |
| `scripts/` | `new_project.py` (the generation driver) and `run_wizard.py` |
| `tests/unit/` | contract tests for the generator: schema validity, key-set match, invalid fixtures failing closed |
| `examples/spike/` | the throwaway spike; present only until the `v0.1.0` tag ([REQ-RUN-0103](requirements.md)) |
| `docs/` | requirements and architecture files; the ADRs are sections of the architecture files (see below) |
| `boundaries/` | one directory per library crate holding its `sc-lint-boundary` manifest ([REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)) |
| `Justfile` | the `just` recipes, including `just new <dest>` |
| `.github/workflows/` | crate CI and the template fixture-matrix CI |

Nothing under `wizard/` or `scripts/` may be placed inside `template/`, so
that no generated project ever contains a wizard or driver file. This item
owns that rule; items about the wizard or the driver refer to it.

Decided in this document: ADRs live in the architecture files (`docs/architecture.md` and `docs/<crate>/architecture.md`).

`examples/spike` is an excluded standalone package while it exists. It is not
a fifth workspace member and it is not a Cargo example. Root `Cargo.toml`
`exclude` names `examples/spike`. The workspace member list is exactly the
library crates in the table above. Sprint a-5 deleted `crates/sc-command/lint-edge/`
when `crates/sc-runtime` landed. `sc-observability` and `sc-observability-otlp`
are not workspace members. `cargo tree` enforces those edges, because sc-lint
0.8.0 rejects a forbidden edge whose target is absent.

statements.text: The GitHub repository `randlee/sc-runtime` MUST contain one Cargo workspace, declared in the root `Cargo.toml`.
The workspace members MUST be exactly these library crates. (see table above)
The repository root MUST also contain the directories and files in the Path/Contents table above.
Each directory and file in the Path/Contents table above MUST NOT be a workspace member.
`template/` MUST NOT be a workspace member.
`template/` MUST NOT be matched by a workspace `members` glob.
The repository MUST NOT contain the sc-runtime design's `docs/adr/` directory.

requirements.rationale:
Keeping the crates and the template in one repository means a crate API
change and the template change that follows it land in one pull request, and
template CI can test the template against the crates at the same commit. How
a generated project is pointed at the checked-out crates is not decided here:
it is the `[patch.crates-io]` question recorded as OPEN in
[REQ-RUN-0003](requirements.md). Keeping `template/` out of the workspace
keeps `cargo build --workspace` working, because the template's Rust files
are not valid Rust until rendered.

The files in `template/` contain `cargo-generate` placeholders and do not compile until rendered. The sc-runtime design's `docs/adr/` directory is not used.

success_criteria.text:
1. Inspect the root `Cargo.toml`: `[workspace] members` is the glob `crates/*`.
   A missing directory is not a member. At the close of sprint `b-1` the glob
   resolves to `crates/sc-config`, `crates/sc-transport`, `crates/sc-command`,
   `crates/sc-runtime`, and `crates/sc-runtime-db-sqlite`. Sprint `b-3` adds
   `crates/sc-cron` and does not edit `Cargo.toml`. The member set is then
   the six crates in the table above.
   `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` lists those packages and
   lists no package whose manifest path is under `template/`. Amended
   2026-10-25.
2. `cargo build --workspace` run at the repository root exits 0 and compiles
   no file under `template/`.
3. Each path in the second table exists at the repository root (with
   `examples/spike/` exempt at and after the `v0.1.0` tag).
4. `find template -path '*wizard*' -o -name 'new_project.py' -o -name
   'run_wizard.py'` prints nothing.
5. `test -d docs/adr` fails (the directory does not exist), and
   `grep -c '^## ADR-' docs/architecture.md` prints a number greater than 0.

requirements.title: Each crate is an independent deliverable

requirement_statement.text:
Definitions: Correct package name metadata is the public crate name in the Phase D package list. Standalone usability means the crate builds and its default-feature tests pass when selected alone, without requiring another SDK crate or the generated application. The pydantic Monty crates implement the pydantic Monty interpreter, including monty and monty-types. Cron types are scheduler, schedule-row and cron-policy types; reserved cron names are cron_stop and cron_tick.

The Phase D public package set is sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-storage and sc-monty, released together at 0.3.0.

Definitions: A tested minimum version is the earliest allowed dependency release validated by the normal build and tests. A registry requirement selects a crate from crates.io. An upper bound restricts dependency releases above that minimum.

statements.text: Each public crate MUST build and pass its own default-feature tests when selected alone from a clean checkout.
Each public crate MUST provide a README whose Rust usage example compiles as a doctest.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its name.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its version.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its description.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its license.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its repository.
Each public crate MUST provide correct package metadata for its readme.
Each public crate MUST be independently publishable to crates.io.
Every published crate MUST declare the MIT license.
The repository LICENSE file MUST contain the MIT license text.
sc-config MUST remain usable without the other SDK crates or generated template.
sc-transport MUST remain usable without the other SDK crates or generated template.
sc-command MUST remain usable without sc-runtime, sc-config, sc-transport or the generated template.
sc-storage MUST use only the Rust standard library.
sc-monty production dependencies MUST be limited to pydantic Monty crates.
sc-cron MUST consume sc-storage for shared storage behavior.
sc-cron MUST consume sc-monty for interpreter behavior.
Published crate registry dependencies MUST declare tested minimum versions with no upper bound.
Template registry dependencies MUST declare tested minimum versions with no upper bound.
Each public crate MUST be published separately to crates.io with its own `cargo publish -p <crate>` operation.
sc-monty MUST NOT have a production dependency on sc-*.
sc-monty MUST NOT have a production dependency on Tokio.
sc-monty MUST NOT have a production dependency on serde_json.
sc-monty MUST NOT define cron types or reserved cron names.

requirements.rationale:
`sc-config` (configuration), `sc-transport` (a local daemon and CLI pair) and
`sc-command` (a JSON-first response envelope) are useful to programs that are
not sc-runtime daemons, so each must stand alone. Independence also means any
crate can move to its own repository later without an API change, and lets a
CLI depend on `sc-transport` and `sc-command` without pulling in the daemon's
dependencies.

success_criteria.text: Normal per-crate tests, README doctests, package metadata inspection and package dry runs verify the public package set. Normal/build dependency graph inspection verifies each crate boundary for its supported features. Pre-publication archive rehearsal qualifies interdependent packages before registry-only proof.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each crate builds and passes its own default-feature tests when selected alone from a clean checkout.
Each crate README usage example passes as a doctest.
Each crate package metadata names its own package and README; its version, description, MIT license and repository identify the published crate rather than incorrectly inherited workspace values.
Each crate passes `cargo publish --dry-run -p <crate>` with exit 0 and no package-metadata warnings.
For each crate, cargo tree inspection covers normal/build dependencies for its supported features, including server-enabled features where available.
Exact package archive rehearsal qualifies dependent crates before registry-only consumer proof.

implementation_notes.text: Generated project licensing remains an independent generation option. Consumers may pin dependencies in their own manifests and locks; this does not permit restrictions in SDK/template dependency declarations. sc-sha is permitted for the cron source key.

requirements.title: Generated projects depend on published versions

requirement_statement.text:
"Generated project" means the Cargo workspace that `cargo generate` renders
from `template/`. "The four crates" means `sc-config`, `sc-transport`,
`sc-command` and `sc-runtime`.

3. This obligation does not apply to a `[patch.crates-io]` table, whose entries are normally `path` or `git` entries. (Path dependencies between the generated project's own crates, such as `daemon` on `service`, are unaffected.)
4. Before a crate's first crates.io publish, and when testing unreleased
   crate changes, the dependency MAY instead be satisfied by a
   `[patch.crates-io]` entry or by a git dependency on a tag of
   `https://github.com/randlee/sc-runtime`. The version requirement in
   obligation 1 stays in place when a `[patch.crates-io]` entry is used. When
   the git form is used, the dependency names the repository URL and a `tag`
   in place of the version requirement.
5. Which generated crate depends on which of the four crates is not stated
   here. It is owned by [REQ-RUN-0301](requirements.md), which holds the
   dependency table of the generated workspace.

Checkout validation MAY satisfy that requirement with the same `[patch.crates-io]` mechanism above; release-mode generation MUST resolve all five crates from the registry without a path or git override.

statements.text: Every `Cargo.toml` rendered into a generated project that depends on one of the four crates MUST name it by a crates.io version requirement (a `version = "..."` key or the bare-string form).

The Phase B continuation extends this requirement to the fifth published crate, `sc-cron`: when the generated daemon enables its optional `cron` feature, every rendered dependency on `sc-cron` MUST retain a crates.io version requirement.
The source of the four crates MUST NOT be copied into a generated project.

A rendered `Cargo.toml` MUST NOT contain a `path = ...` dependency on any of the four crates in a dependency table (`[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]`, `[workspace.dependencies]` or a `[target.*]` form of these).

requirements.rationale:
Generated code cannot be upgraded after it is created; a versioned dependency
can, with `cargo update`. A path dependency or a copy of the crate source
inside each project would mean every fix has to be re-applied by hand in
every project. Everyone who owns a generated project is affected.

success_criteria.text:
1. For every answers file in `wizard/fixtures/`, render the project and
   inspect every rendered `Cargo.toml`: each dependency on `sc-config`,
   `sc-transport`, `sc-command` or `sc-runtime` has a version requirement,
   or, where the git form of obligation 4 is in use, a `git` URL of
   `https://github.com/randlee/sc-runtime` with a `tag`.
2. In the same rendered files, `grep -n 'path *='` finds no line belonging
   to a dependency on any of the four crates outside a `[patch.crates-io]`
   table.
3. The rendered project contains no directory named `sc-config`,
   `sc-transport`, `sc-command` or `sc-runtime`.
4. A release-mode render with generated feature `cron` names `sc-cron` by
   version, contains no path/git override for any of the five crates, and
   resolves all five from the registry.

key_considerations:
OPEN: who writes the `[patch.crates-io]` entry in the pre-publish case
(a template option, the driver `scripts/new_project.py`, or the CI workflow)
is not decided. The same undecided mechanism is what would let template CI
build a generated project against the crates of the checkout under test
([REQ-RUN-0701](requirements.md)).

OPEN: the form of the version requirement (for example caret on the
minor version) is not decided.

requirements.title: Root `justfile` recipes `lint`, `test` and `new`

requirement_statement.text:
Definitions: SC base commands are the standard lint and test recipe names supplied by the sc-lint tooling adopted in this repository.

That is the name `sc-lint init --just` writes. The first line stays the sc-lint init header.

| Recipe | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `just lint` | Runs every static check for this repository and exits non-zero if any check fails. It MUST include the `sc-lint-boundary` check ([REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)) and the `sc-lint` source file length check, 1000 source lines not counting blank and comment-only lines ([NFR-RUN-0008](requirements.md)). |
| `just test` | Runs every command of the `just test` list below, and exits non-zero if any of them fails. |
| `just new <dest>` | Runs the generation driver `scripts/new_project.py` with `<dest>` as the destination directory of the new project. Any further arguments (for example `--var-file <answers.json>` or `--prefill <json>`) MUST be passed through to the driver unchanged. |

The list is decided in this document; the sc-runtime design names only the recipe.

1. `cargo test --workspace --exclude sc-cron` (Monty needs rustc 1.96; see items 2 and 6).
2. `cargo test -p sc-cron` with default features.
3. `cargo test -p sc-config`, `cargo test -p sc-transport`,
   `cargo test -p sc-command` and `cargo test -p sc-runtime`, each with
   default cargo features. These are needed because `cargo test --workspace`
   builds `sc-transport` and `sc-command` once with their `server` feature
   on (`sc-runtime` enables it, and cargo unifies features across the
   packages it builds together), so it never tests their default-feature
   build.
4. `cargo test -p sc-transport --features server` and
   `cargo test -p sc-command --features server`.
5. The generator contract tests under `tests/unit/`.
6. `cargo test -p sc-cron --features monty` on **rustc 1.96** (the `monty`
   1.4 crates require 1.96; workspace MSRV stays 1.94.1 for the other crates).

There is exactly one recorded exception: the job required by [REQ-RUN-0306](requirements.md), which proves that plain `cargo generate` works without the driver, and therefore runs `cargo generate --path template ...` and `cargo build --workspace` directly.

`just lint` with no profile runs the sc-lint 0.8.6 full profile through
`.sc-lint/bootstrap.py` and `sc-lint.toml`: `sc-lint lint sc-boundary` (the
`boundary` lint), line-counts, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy --workspace --exclude sc-cron --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
`cargo clippy -p sc-cron --all-targets --features monty -- -D warnings` on
**rustc 1.96**. `just lint gates`
is the early profile of boundary plus line-counts. The line-counts key is
`[line_counts] max_production_lines` and its value is `1000` for non-test
files under `crates/*/src`. `template/**/*.rs` is not configured in this
sprint.

statements.text: The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of the `randlee/sc-runtime` repository MUST define the `lint` recipe described in the table above.
The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of the `randlee/sc-runtime` repository MUST define the `test` recipe described in the table above.
The file `Justfile` (capital J) at the root of the `randlee/sc-runtime` repository MUST define the `new` recipe described in the table above.
`just test` MUST run all of these.
Decided in this document: every job in `.github/workflows/` that lints, tests or generates MUST do so by calling one of these recipes, not by calling `cargo`, `python` or a lint tool directly.
A workflow file under `.github/workflows/` (the crate CI workflow) MUST run `just lint` and `just test` at the repository root on every pull request.
The standard `sc-lint` base command names `lint` and `test` MUST NOT be renamed or aliased to other primary names.

requirements.rationale:
Every SC repository exposes the same base `just` commands so that agents, CI
and people use one vocabulary and need no per-repository knowledge to lint or
test. Routing CI through the same recipes means a green local `just lint` and
`just test` predicts a green CI run.

success_criteria.text:
1. `just --list` at the repository root shows `lint`, `test` and `new`.
2. `just lint` and `just test` each exit 0 on a clean checkout of the default
   branch.
3. Introducing a failing unit test in any workspace crate makes `just test`
   exit non-zero; introducing a failing test under `tests/unit/` does the
   same.
4. Introducing, in `crates/sc-command`, a failing test gated with
   `#[cfg(not(feature = "server"))]` makes `just test` exit non-zero, and so
   does a failing test gated with `#[cfg(feature = "server")]`. This shows
   both feature configurations are tested.
5. `just new <dest> --var-file wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json` invokes
   `scripts/new_project.py` with that destination and that `--var-file`
   argument (check by inspecting the recipe body).
6. Inspect every file in `.github/workflows/`: each lint, test or generate
   step is a `just lint`, `just test` or `just new` invocation, except the
   steps of the one plain-`cargo generate` job of
   [REQ-RUN-0306](requirements.md).
7. One workflow file under `.github/workflows/` has a `pull_request` trigger
   and steps running `just lint` and `just test` at the repository root, and
   a pull request's check list shows a run of that workflow.

requirements.title: Boundary manifests for every crate

requirement_statement.text:
Definitions: For this requirement, workspace crates are sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-runtime-db-sqlite and sc-cron (the last two included by the 2026-10-25 amendment). A boundary manifest consists of one or more TOML files under boundaries/<crate>/ at the repository root in the format read by sc-lint-boundary. The path placeholder <crate> is the workspace crate name. sc-lint-boundary is the dependency-boundary checker invoked by sc-lint; sc-lint is the repository lint tool. TOML is the manifest data format with the keys listed below.

Definitions: A boundary manifest is one or more TOML files declaring public facade items, allowed dependencies, allowed dependents and forbidden dependency edges for sc-lint-boundary. A workspace crate is a library crate listed in the root Cargo workspace.

Definitions: ATM denotes agent-team-mail, agent-team-mail-core and atm-* tool packages and their corresponding Rust library imports, including atm_core. The crate graph is the set of workspace dependency edges and forbidden edges in the table below. A crate's additional allowed dependency list is the list owned by its referenced per-crate requirement, combined with that crate's table row.

This requirement is decided in this document; the sc-runtime design does not
state it.

2. The manifest format, as observed in the sc-lint repository, is TOML with these keys: `boundary_id`, `owner_package`, a `[public]` table with `facade`, an `[implementation]` table, a `[composition]` table with `roots`, a `[dependencies]` table with `allowed_dependents`, `allowed_dependencies` and `forbidden_edges` (each forbidden edge a string of the form `"a -> b"`), and a `[references]` table.
3. This item owns the edges among all workspace library crates and the forbidden edges.

   | Crate | Workspace crates it depends on | Forbidden edges (`forbidden_edges`) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `sc-config` | none | `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`, `sc-observability-types`, `tokio` |
   | `sc-transport` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`, `sc-observability-types` |
   | `sc-command` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp` |
   | `sc-runtime` | MUST: `sc-transport` with its `server` cargo feature, `sc-command` with its `server` cargo feature, and `sc-observability-types` for the injected canonical logger contract. The edge `sc-runtime` -> `sc-config` is absent | `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sqlx` (cargo tree; not a workspace member), `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp` |
| `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-cron`. `sqlx` is absent and is checked with `cargo tree`, because it is not a workspace member |
| `sc-cron` | MUST: registry `sc-observability-types`; TEMPORARY `sc-command` 0.1.1, defaults off/no features, for the contract (ADR-RUN-0017) | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`. `sqlx` is absent and is checked with `cargo tree` |
| `sc-cron-commands` (Phase C target) | defaults-off `sc-command`; optional `sc-cron` under non-default scheduler feature | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, full observability/OTLP and production tool crates |

Phase C also forbids sc-command→sc-cron-commands and
sc-runtime→sc-cron-commands. The adapter is an allowed dependent of command
and, only with scheduler enabled, cron. These planned edges are implemented
by c-1 boundary manifests and checked by c-6/c-4 isolated graph tests.

`sc-observability-types` is an allowed dependency of `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and `sc-cron`; the latter two import the temporary command contract and direct canonical values under ADR-RUN-0017. The full `sc-observability` runtime remains forbidden in every library crate. Boundary lint rejects production edges/imports; companion production cargo-tree checks cover renamed or transitive external packages that the workspace-only boundary tool cannot inspect. The rule applies to every supported production feature combination and to normal/build dependency edges. Dev-only test and benchmark references are permitted. Invoking either external CLI through an application-configured host adapter remains permitted and does not link its Rust crate. Package identity, rather than dependency-key spelling, governs this rule: known tool packages include `sc-compose`, `sc-compose-*`, `agent-team-mail`, `agent-team-mail-core`, and `atm-*`; imports include the corresponding Rust library names such as `sc_compose` and `atm_core`. Renaming a dependency must not bypass the production exclusion. Test fixtures exercise those names and renamed equivalents instead of relying only on an `atm` prefix match.

The table lists the full forbidden-edge policy. Manifest `forbidden_edges`
list only workspace-member targets in that lint tree; crates.io names use
criterion 5 `cargo tree` checks. sc-lint 0.8.0 cannot fail a crates.io edge,
so b-13's types-only rule is measured with direct-depth `cargo tree` checks
for `sc-runtime` and `sc-cron`; each may print `sc-observability-types ` but
must print no direct `sc-observability ` or `sc-observability-otlp ` line.
`allowed_dependents` is empty for `sc-config`, `sc-runtime`,
`sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, and `sc-cron`; it is `sc-runtime` for
`sc-transport`, and temporarily runtime+cron for `sc-command` under ADR-RUN-0017. The edge `sc-runtime` -> `sc-config` is absent, so it is not an
`allowed_dependents` entry and it is a `forbidden_edges` entry
`sc-runtime -> sc-config`. The measurement is the sprint a-1 evidence record
for the other edges, and sprint a-5 for this absent edge.

4. This item does not list the third-party crates each crate may depend on.
5. The manifest format has no key for cargo features, so `sc-lint-boundary`
   enforces only the inter-crate edges and the public facade list. The three
   kinds of rule are enforced as follows:

   | Rule | Enforced by |
   |---|---|
   | inter-crate edges and forbidden edges; public facade list | `sc-lint-boundary`, run by `just lint` |
   | dependencies allowed only behind the `server` cargo feature (`axum` in `sc-transport`; `axum` and `rmcp` in `sc-command`) | the `cargo tree` criteria of [NFR-TRN-0001](sc-transport/requirements.md), [NFR-CMD-0001](sc-command/requirements.md) and [NFR-RUN-0001](requirements.md) |
   | `sc-runtime` wraps no `axum` or `rmcp` type ([NFR-RT-0001](sc-runtime/requirements.md)) | architecture review of the pull request |

The manifest file name is `boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml`.

The edge `sc-runtime -> sc-config` is absent. `sc-runtime` does not depend on
`sc-config` and does not load configuration. `boundaries/sc-runtime/sc-runtime.toml`
lists `sc-runtime -> sc-config` under `forbidden_edges`.

[ADR-RUN-0003](architecture.md) and the crate graph in `docs/architecture.md` mirror the table.

Each additional allowed dependency list is owned by that crate's own requirement.

ADR-RUN-0017 permits the cron-to-command edge with defaults disabled and no features. All other tool-crate exclusions remain. Direct-depth normal-only checks below are historical minimum checks and do not prove the full normal/build dependency closure. The edge tables describe existing code and stay enforced until that code changes. PRD v2.0 changes the storage edges when implemented: sc-cron drops rusqlite and stores its table through Storage<CronRow>, and the SQLite writer is permitted in the template. The four-crate prohibition retained by ADR-RUN-0012 still governs SDK dependencies on that writer.

statements.text: The repository MUST contain a boundary manifest for each workspace crate.
Each manifest MUST record the crate's public facade (the items it exports) in `[public] facade`.
Each manifest MUST record the crate's allowed dependents in `[dependencies]`.
Each manifest MUST record the crate's allowed dependencies in `[dependencies]`.
Each manifest MUST record the crate's forbidden edges in `[dependencies]`.
The manifests MUST encode exactly the table above.
In addition to the table, every production release crate (`sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and `sc-cron`) MUST exclude sc-compose crate dependencies.
In addition to the table, every production release crate (`sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and `sc-cron`) MUST exclude ATM crate dependencies.
In addition to the table, every production release crate (`sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and `sc-cron`) MUST exclude sc-compose Rust imports.
In addition to the table, every production release crate (`sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and `sc-cron`) MUST exclude ATM Rust imports.

The manifest's `allowed_dependencies` MUST equal the row above plus that list: [NFR-CFG-0002](sc-config/requirements.md) for `sc-config`, [NFR-TRN-0001](sc-transport/requirements.md) for `sc-transport`, [NFR-CMD-0001](sc-command/requirements.md) for `sc-command`, [NFR-RT-0003](sc-runtime/requirements.md) for `sc-runtime`, [NFR-CRON-0001](sc-cron/requirements.md) for `sc-cron`, and [REQ-DBSQ-0001](sc-runtime-db-sqlite/requirements.md) for `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`.
The `just lint` recipe in the root `Justfile` MUST run `sc-lint lint sc-boundary` against these manifests.

The normal/build dependency closures of sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime and sc-cron MUST exclude the full sc-observability logger and sc-observability-otlp packages by resolved identity, including aliases and transitive edges.

requirements.rationale:
Two properties of the crate graph are the ones most likely to erode without
anyone noticing: there is no dependency edge among `sc-config`,
`sc-transport` and `sc-command`, and nothing server-side (`axum`, `rmcp`,
`sqlx`) is reachable from a CLI build. One convenient `use` breaks either, so
they are checked mechanically and not left to review: the first by
`sc-lint-boundary` on every lint run, the second by `cargo tree` criteria,
because the manifest format cannot express a cargo feature. Keeping the edge
table in one item stops the copies in the ADR and in the crate files from
drifting apart. The manifests also tell sprint planning which crates can be
built in parallel without touching each other.

requirements.title: Spike `examples/spike` proves the stack coexists

requirement_statement.text:
`examples/spike` in the `randlee/sc-runtime` repository is a throwaway proof,
built before any of the four library crates exists, so it uses the third-party
crates directly.

Definitions: MCP is Model Context Protocol, served by rmcp. A custom connector is application-written transport connection code instead of reqwest ClientBuilder::unix_socket(path). The one service function is the spike async function that accesses SQLite.

Database access here means reading or writing that SQLite database.

statements.text: The spike MUST contain one server binary that uses a single `axum` 0.8 `Router` in a single process.
The spike server MUST register REST routes through `utoipa-axum` 0.2 `OpenApiRouter` with the `routes!` macro.
The spike server MUST mount an `rmcp` 3.x `StreamableHttpService` in stateless mode with `Router::nest_service("/mcp", service)`.
The spike server MUST open a SQLite database through `sqlx` 0.9 with the `sqlite` feature.
The spike server MUST pass a Unix domain socket listener (`tokio::net::UnixListener`) to `axum::serve`.
The spike MUST contain exactly one async service function that accesses the SQLite database.
The REST handler MUST call the one async service function that reads or writes the SQLite database.
The MCP tool MUST call the one async service function that reads or writes the SQLite database.
The spike MUST contain a `clap` command-line client.
The spike `clap` client MUST connect to the server socket using `reqwest` 0.13 `ClientBuilder::unix_socket(path)`.
The spike `clap` client MUST call the REST route.
Against one running spike server process, `curl --unix-socket <path>` calling the REST route MUST reach the one async SQLite service function.
Against one running spike server process, the `clap` client MUST reach the one async SQLite service function.
Against one running spike server process, an MCP client issuing `tools/call` on `/mcp` MUST reach the one async SQLite service function.
The REST handler MUST NOT contain SQL.
The MCP tool MUST NOT contain SQL.
The spike MUST NOT use `hyperlocal`.
The spike MUST NOT use a custom connector.

requirements.rationale:
The whole architecture assumes that `axum`, `utoipa-axum`, `rmcp` and `sqlx`
share one router, one listener and one process, and that a CLI can reach that
listener over a Unix socket with stock `reqwest`. If any of that is false the
crate split and the template are wrong. Half a day of spike proves it before
four crates and a template are built on the assumption.

success_criteria.text:
1. `cargo build` of `examples/spike` exits 0 with `axum`, `utoipa-axum`,
   `rmcp`, `sqlx` and `reqwest` in one dependency graph; the output of
   `cargo tree -i axum` for the spike package is recorded and shows exactly
   one `axum` version.
2. With the spike server running, `curl --unix-socket <socket> ...` on the
   REST route returns HTTP 200 and the operation's result.
3. With the same server process, the `clap` client returns the same
   operation's result and exits 0.
4. With the same server process, an MCP `tools/call` request to `/mcp`
   returns the same operation's result.
5. Inspect the spike source: one service function contains the only SQL; the
   REST handler and the MCP tool each call it.
6. The commands run for criteria 2 to 4 and their output are recorded in
   `docs/architecture.md` together with the evidence required by
   [REQ-RUN-0102](requirements.md).

key_considerations:
OPEN: what the spike's one operation does, its route path and its MCP
tool name are not stated; any single operation that touches SQLite satisfies
this requirement.

OPEN: which MCP client is used for the proof is not stated; any client
that speaks MCP Streamable HTTP over the Unix socket qualifies.

requirements.title: Spike answers the four unverified facts and pins versions

requirement_statement.text:
Definitions: MCP is Model Context Protocol. A tools/list surface snapshot is a recorded dump of the MCP server tools/list response. Snapshot dumping is the fifth verification item that was removed from the spike investigation.

The sc-runtime design relies on four facts it has not verified.

This table is the only definition of that evidence. ADR-RUN-0203 and
ADR-RUN-0402, both Active after sprint a-1, refer to its rows by id. Any
text beside a row id in those ADRs is a non-normative summary; the rows of
this item govern.

| Row | Fact to verify | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| V1 | `rmcp` 3.x, `utoipa-axum` 0.2 and `axum` 0.8 coexist on one `axum::Router` with no dependency version conflict. | `examples/spike` compiles with all three in one binary; `cargo tree -i axum` run on the spike package shows exactly one `axum` version; with the spike running, `curl --unix-socket`, the `clap` client and an MCP client each reach the one service function through that one router ([REQ-RUN-0101](requirements.md)). |
| V2 | `rmcp`'s `Parameters<T>` accepts a struct `T` that derives both `schemars::JsonSchema` and `utoipa::ToSchema`, with no clash between the two derives or their schemas. | The spike's request struct derives `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `schemars::JsonSchema` and `utoipa::ToSchema`; it is used as an `axum` `Json<T>` body and as `Parameters<T>` in a `#[tool]`; it compiles and both calls answer; MCP `tools/list` returns an input schema for that tool, and `openapi.json` contains the same struct as a component schema. |
| V3a | The `cargo-generate` version pinned by sprint a-1 accepts, in `cargo-generate.toml`, placeholders of type `string`, `bool` and `array`, a conditional `ignore` list keyed on a placeholder value, and an `exclude` list; the exact syntax of each is known. | A scratch `cargo-generate.toml` using every one of these constructs, copied into the record, that the pinned version parses without error. |
| V3b | A conditional `ignore` list includes or excludes a whole file. | Two runs of the scratch template that differ only in one `bool` value: the conditionally ignored file is present in one output and absent in the other. |
| V4a | `cargo generate --path <template> --template-values-file <file> --name <n> --silent` runs with no prompt, including when a value is of type `array`. | The command line used; run with stdin closed it exits 0 and prints no prompt, and the rendered output contains the `string`, `bool` and `array` values from the values file. |
| V4b | A file listed under `exclude` (for example `AGENTS.md.j2`) is copied byte-for-byte without Liquid rendering. | A `.j2` file containing `{{ }}` expressions is byte-identical in the template and in the generated output (`cmp` exits 0). |

ADR-RUN-0203 and ADR-RUN-0402 were the two `Proposed` ADRs, and each held
nothing but unverified facts. Sprint a-1 made both `Active`:

| ADR | Holds | Rests on rows |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-RUN-0203](architecture.md) | that the pinned `rmcp`, `utoipa-axum` and `axum` versions coexist, and that one struct is both the `Parameters<T>` input and a `ToSchema` type; the version pins | V1, V2 |
| [ADR-RUN-0402](architecture.md) | the `cargo-generate` mechanics: conditional `ignore`, `exclude`, the non-interactive values file, the `cargo-generate.toml` syntax and the `cargo-generate` version pin | V3a, V3b, V4a, V4b |

Sprint a-1 moved both from `Proposed` to `Active`. Every row was true, so the
Decision text did not have to be replaced by a different mechanism. The
working cargo-generate syntax, including the array-`default` constraint, is
recorded in ADR-RUN-0402.

The shape decisions do not wait for the spike and are already `Active`:
[ADR-RUN-0202](architecture.md) (REST, OpenAPI and MCP on one `axum` router
and one listener) and [ADR-RUN-0401](architecture.md) (the generation
pipeline and the `answers.schema.json` contract). If V1 or V2 is false, the
pinned versions change, not the one-router shape.

Decided in this document: the sc-runtime design's Phase 0 exit gate "ADR
amendments written and accepted" is met by
[ADR-RUN-0001](architecture.md) (which amends SC scaffold ADR-013, the
single assembly point and command registry) and
[ADR-RUN-0201](architecture.md) (which carries SC scaffold ADR-014, the
daemon is always running) having Status `Active` in `docs/architecture.md`.
ADRs live in the architecture files; the design's `docs/adr/` directory is
not used.

statements.text: The spike sprint MUST record the MCP `tools/list` snapshot-dumping verification item as closed without investigation.
The spike sprint MUST also record the exact version used for each of `axum`, `utoipa`, `utoipa-axum`, `rmcp`, `sqlx`, `reqwest` and `cargo-generate`.
All evidence and version pins MUST be written into `docs/architecture.md`.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V1.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V1 for that outcome.
When row V1 is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V2.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V2 for that outcome.
When row V2 is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V3a.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V3a for that outcome.
When row V3a is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V3b.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V3b for that outcome.
When row V3b is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V4a.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V4a for that outcome.
When row V4a is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.
The spike sprint, named sprint a-1 (the work in `examples/spike` plus a scratch `cargo-generate` template), MUST record a Boolean outcome for row V4b.
The spike sprint MUST record the evidence required by row V4b for that outcome.
When row V4b is false, the spike sprint MUST record what was found instead.

requirements.rationale:
These facts fix the dependency versions every crate uses and the template
syntax every template file uses. Planning later sprints around a guess would
turn each wrong guess into rework across four crates and the template, so
nothing may be planned around them as facts until the spike has answered
them.

Snapshot tooling is not part of this repository.

success_criteria.text:
1. `docs/architecture.md` contains, for each of the six rows V1, V2, V3a,

2. `docs/architecture.md` records that the MCP `tools/list` dump question is

3. `docs/architecture.md` lists an exact version (`major.minor.patch`) for

5. For each row answered false, the Decision text of the ADR that rests on
