requirements.title: `sc-command` dependency boundary

requirement_statement.text:
2026-10-31 amendment: command remains a sibling-free leaf; its sole
additional dependent is temporarily cron for the observability port with
defaults off/no features. Full-runtime/OTLP exclusions cover normal/build
transitive identities for every production feature, not just direct normal edges.

These rules apply to every feature combination, including `server`.

`cargo tree` enforces the logging crates and the sibling crates.
`sc-observability-types` is an allowed dependency and is not a forbidden
edge. sc-lint 0.8.0 rejects a forbidden edge whose target is not a workspace
member, so `forbidden_edges` does not name `sc-observability` or
`sc-observability-otlp`. `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, and
`sc-runtime-db-sqlite` are workspace members, so
`boundaries/sc-command/sc-command.toml` lists those edges under
`forbidden_edges` ([REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md)). `sc-cron` stays off
that list until it is a workspace member. Cargo.toml inspection and
`cargo tree` still enforce the sibling edges. `allowed_dependents` is temporarily
`sc-runtime` plus `sc-cron` under ADR-RUN-0017; command remains a leaf. Sprint a-5 deleted `crates/sc-command/lint-edge/` when `crates/sc-runtime`
landed. The third-party crates
`sc-command` may depend on are listed in [NFR-CMD-0001](requirements.md).
`sc-lint lint sc-boundary` checks inter-crate edges and the public facade
list only; it has no cargo-feature key, so the feature-conditional
dependencies on axum and rmcp are checked with `cargo tree`.

statements.text: `sc-command` MUST depend on the published crate `sc-observability-types` at exact `=1.5.0` during the ADR-RUN-0017 bridge; remove this temporary pin when the actual upstream capability is consumed.
`sc-command` MUST NOT depend on any other crate of this workspace: `sc-config`, `sc-transport` or `sc-runtime`.
`sc-command` MUST NOT depend, directly or transitively, on the crate `sc-observability` (the logging runtime) or on its OTel export crate `sc-observability-otlp`.

requirements.rationale:
Each library crate in this repository is an independent deliverable,
published to crates.io and usable without the others
([REQ-RUN-0002](../requirements.md)); an edge to a sibling crate would force
every user of the envelope to take that sibling too. The three standalone
crates have no edges among them and only `sc-runtime` knows the others
([ADR-RUN-0003](../architecture.md)). Observability is initialised directly
by each project and is not wrapped by these crates; the single permitted
observability dependency is the types-only crate, because the envelope's
error code and remediation types are defined there
([ADR-RUN-0004](../architecture.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. Inspection of `crates/sc-command/Cargo.toml`: none of `sc-config`,
   `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-observability`,
   `sc-observability-otlp` appears in `[dependencies]`,
   `[dev-dependencies]` or `[build-dependencies]`;
   `sc-observability-types` appears in `[dependencies]`.
2. `cargo tree -p sc-command -e normal --prefix none` (default features)
   prints no line beginning with `sc-config `, `sc-transport `,
   `sc-runtime `, `sc-observability ` or `sc-observability-otlp ` (each name
   followed by a space, so that `sc-observability-types` and the repository
   path do not match), and prints a line beginning with
   `sc-observability-types `.
3. `cargo tree -p sc-command -e normal --prefix none --features server`
   gives the same result as criterion 2.
4. This sprint's boundary check is `sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root .` on
   `boundaries/sc-command/sc-command.toml`. Root `just lint` across all four
   manifests stays with sprint a-5.

requirements.title: `sc-command` never panics; `into_mcp` error exception

requirement_statement.text:
2026-10-31 explicit exception: ADR-RUN-0017 allows only the fixed
`ServiceName::new("noop")` invariant under exact inspected types 1.5.0,
never caller/environment data. `CanonicalLog::emit` returns canonical foreign
EventError. The rest of this panic/error rule remains in force; moving an
existing expect into command without this amendment would violate it.

No public function, method or trait implementation of `sc-command` may panic
on any caller input. This covers constructors of `Envelope<T>` and
`OpError`, `From<Result<T, OpError>> for Envelope<T>`, the serde
implementations, `IntoResponse::into_response` for `Envelope<T>`, and
`IntoMcp::into_mcp`.

There is no allowance for a commented exception. Test code (`#[cfg(test)]` modules and `crates/sc-command/tests/`) is exempt. This item adds only the `sc-command`-specific points below.

The same repository rule requires a fallible public function to return
`Result<T, E>` where `E` is a typed error enum owned by the crate
(`ConfigError`, `TransportError` and `RuntimeError` in the other three
crates). It applies to errors a crate itself originates, and it is decided
in this document for `sc-command` (the design states it for `sc-config`
only). Two `sc-command` signatures are the recorded exception, because a
third-party crate dictates them: `sc_command::IntoMcp::into_mcp` returns
`Result<CallToolResult, McpError>` with rmcp's `ErrorData` (imported as
`McpError`), which is what an rmcp `#[tool]` function must return; and
axum's `IntoResponse::into_response` is infallible. `into_mcp` is the only
fallible public function this document requires of `sc-command`. v0.1 does
not add an `sc-command` error enum. No function required by
[REQ-CMD-0001](requirements.md) through [REQ-CMD-0006](requirements.md)
originates an error other than through serde or rmcp.

statements.text: A failure inside a conversion, in particular a `T` whose `Serialize` implementation returns an error, MUST surface as a returned value: HTTP 500 with code `ENVELOPE.SERIALIZATION` from `into_response`, and `Err(McpError)` from `into_mcp`.

The repository-wide rule is owned by [NFR-RUN-0009](../requirements.md) and applies to `crates/sc-command/src` unchanged: non-test code MUST NOT contain `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, or panicking `[]` indexing, reachable from a public function.

requirements.rationale:
These conversions run inside the request handlers of a long-lived daemon. A
panic there aborts the request, or the whole process under some panic
settings, and the client receives no envelope it can parse. Library errors
in this repository are typed values, not panics
([ADR-RUN-0006](../architecture.md)). The exception for `into_mcp` and
`into_response` is recorded here so that a reviewer applying the typed-enum
rule does not reject the two signatures that rmcp and axum require.

success_criteria.text:
1. `grep -rnE '\.unwrap\(|\.expect\(|panic!|unreachable!|todo!|unimplemented!' crates/sc-command/src`
   returns no match outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules, and no match is excused
   by a comment.
2. Source review of `crates/sc-command/src` finds no `[...]` indexing on a
   slice, `Vec` or map in non-test code.
3. A test compiled with `--features server` defines a type whose
   `Serialize` implementation always returns an error, wraps it in a
   success envelope, calls `.into_response()`, and completes without
   panicking.
4. A test calls `.into_mcp()` on `Ok(value)` of that same type and
   completes without panicking.
5. Inspection of the public API of `crates/sc-command/src`: apart from the
   `serde::Serialize` and `serde::Deserialize` implementations, whose error
   types serde dictates, the only public function returning a `Result` is
   `IntoMcp::into_mcp`, and its error type is rmcp's `McpError`.

requirements.title: `load` merges `default.json` and `local.json`

requirement_statement.text:
This item covers the file layer of the `sc-config` crate (`crates/sc-config`).
The design fixes the two file names and that `local.json` is gitignored. The
merge rules below are decided in this document.

```rust
pub fn load<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(app: AppName) -> Result<T, ConfigError>
```

`app` is an `sc_config::AppName`. Callers construct it with `AppName::new` or
`TryFrom<&str>`. A name that is empty, longer than 64 bytes, or outside ASCII
letters, digits, `-`, and `_` fails in that constructor with
`ConfigError::InvalidName` and stable code `APP.INVALID_NAME`. It does not
reach `load`. The name still selects only the environment-variable prefix
(entry 9). Display is `as_str` or `AsRef<str>`. The type does not implement
`Deref`.

4. The result is then built from `config/default.json` alone.
7. Those overrides take precedence over both files ([REQ-CFG-0002](requirements.md)).
9. It selects only the environment-variable prefix.

`merge(base, overlay)`, decided in this document:

| `base` is | `overlay` is | Result |
|---|---|---|
| JSON object | JSON object | An object holding every key of `base` and every key of `overlay`. A key present in both has the value `merge(base[key], overlay[key])`. |
| anything | string, number, boolean, array or `null` | `overlay`. Arrays are replaced whole; array elements are never merged or appended. `null` replaces the value; it does not delete the key. |
| string, number, boolean, array or `null` | JSON object | `overlay`. |

Precedence, lowest to highest: `config/default.json`, `config/local.json`,
environment variables.

Worked example. `config/default.json`:

```json
{
  "daemon": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 7400 },
  "logging": { "level": "info", "targets": ["stdout", "file"] },
  "stores": { "sqlite": { "path": "data/app.db" } }
}
```

`config/local.json`:

```json
{
  "daemon": { "port": 9000 },
  "logging": { "level": null, "targets": ["stdout"] },
  "stores": "disabled"
}
```

Merged value, with no environment overrides set:

```json
{
  "daemon": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 9000 },
  "logging": { "level": null, "targets": ["stdout"] },
  "stores": "disabled"
}
```

`daemon.host` survives because objects merge key by key. `logging.targets` is
replaced, not concatenated. `logging.level` becomes `null`. `stores` changes
from an object to a string because a non-object overlay replaces whatever is
beneath it.

statements.text: The crate MUST export this function:
`load` MUST read `config/default.json`, resolved against the process's current working directory.
`config/default.json` MUST exist.
If it does not, `load` MUST return the `ConfigError` variant for a missing default file ([REQ-CFG-0004](requirements.md)).
`load` MUST read `config/local.json` from the same directory when that file exists.
Each file MUST be read as bytes and parsed as one JSON document into a `serde_json::Value` (`serde_json::from_slice`).
`load` MUST merge the `local.json` value over the `default.json` value with the function `merge(base, overlay)` defined in the table below. (see table above)
`load` MUST then apply the environment-variable overrides of app `app` to the merged value.
`load` MUST deserialise the final value into `T` exactly once, with `serde_json::from_value::<T>`.
An absent `config/local.json` MUST NOT be an error.
The `app` argument MUST NOT change which files are read.
`load` MUST NOT write, create or modify any file.

requirements.rationale:
`config/default.json` is checked in and documents every setting.
`config/local.json` is gitignored and holds one machine's differences.
Recursive object merge lets `local.json` change one nested key without
restating its siblings, so a developer's local file stays a few lines long.
Replacing arrays whole avoids the question of how two lists combine, which has
no answer that suits every setting. The design fixes the two file names and
says nothing about merge semantics; this item decides them so that every
project built on `sc-config` layers its files the same way.

success_criteria.text:
All tests live in `crates/sc-config` and compare `serde_json::Value`s for
equality, so key order is irrelevant.

1. A unit test writes the `default.json` and `local.json` of the worked example
   into a temporary directory, loads with an empty environment into
   `serde_json::Value`, and asserts the result equals the merged value shown
   above.
2. A unit test with only `default.json` present asserts the load succeeds and
   the result equals the content of `default.json`.
3. A unit test with `default.json` `{"a":[1,2,3]}` and `local.json`
   `{"a":[9]}` asserts the result is `{"a":[9]}`.
4. A unit test with `default.json` `{"a":{"b":1,"c":2}}` and `local.json`
   `{"a":{"b":null}}` asserts the result is `{"a":{"b":null,"c":2}}`.
5. A unit test with `default.json` `{"a":1}` and `local.json` `{"a":{"b":2}}`
   asserts the result is `{"a":{"b":2}}`.
6. A unit test with `default.json` `{"a":1}`, `local.json` `{"a":2}` and an
   environment override that sets `a` to `3` asserts the result is `{"a":3}`.
7. A unit test with no `default.json` in the directory asserts the result is
   `Err` with the missing-default-file variant
   ([REQ-CFG-0004](requirements.md)).
8. A unit test lists the temporary config directory before and after a load
   and asserts the file names and file contents are unchanged.
9. A unit test loads one temporary config directory twice with an empty
   environment, once for app `my-app` and once for app `other-app`, and
   asserts the two results are equal: the app name does not change which
   files are read (entry 9).

requirements.title: Environment overrides named `APP__KEY__KEY`

requirement_statement.text:
This item covers the environment layer of the `sc-config` crate
(`crates/sc-config`). The design fixes only that JSON config files have
environment-variable overrides. The naming scheme, the value parsing and the
path rules below are decided in this document.

Overrides are applied to the `serde_json::Value` produced by merging
`config/default.json` and `config/local.json`
([REQ-CFG-0001](requirements.md)), before that value is deserialised into the
caller's type.

Variable name:

1. App `my-app` gives prefix `MY_APP__`. `_` is already that character, so `my_app` yields the same prefix. `AppName::env_prefix` is the function that implements this rule.
2. The comparison is exact and case-sensitive. Empty segments, application order, and non-Unicode names or values are decided below.
3. `OTHER_APP__DAEMON__PORT` and `MY_APP_DAEMON_PORT` (single underscores) are both ignored for app `my-app`.
5. The segments, in order, are the key path. `MY_APP__DAEMON__MAX_CONNECTIONS` addresses key `max_connections` inside object `daemon`.
6. It is part of the key.
7. A key that contains an ASCII upper-case letter, or that contains `__`,
   cannot be addressed by an override. Array elements cannot be addressed; an
   array is overridden whole.

Value:

9. `8080` is a number, `true` is a boolean, `null` is JSON null, `["a"]` is an array, `{"x":1}` is an object and `"8080"` (with the quotes) is the string `8080`.
10. `debug` becomes `"debug"`, `0.0.0.0` becomes `"0.0.0.0"` and the empty value becomes `""`.

Applying an override with key path `k1, k2, ..., kn`:

11. The walk then moves to the value at that key.
13. An existing value at `kn` is replaced whole, whatever its type. An override value that is an object replaces; it is not merged.

Decided: An application name is `sc_config::AppName`, not a free `&str`.
`AppName::new` accepts only ASCII `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, and `_`, length 1
through 64 bytes. Every other string is `ConfigError::InvalidName` with code
`APP.INVALID_NAME`. The only accept and reject list is
`tests/fixtures/app-name-vectors.json`.

Decided: An empty path segment is the cannot-be-applied failure
(`ConfigError::Override`, code `CFG.OVERRIDE`). `MY_APP__`, `MY_APP__A____B`,
and `MY_APP__A__` each return that variant and carry the variable name. The
variable is not ignored.

Decided: Matching variables are applied in ascending order of the
variable name's encoded bytes. Process-environment order is not used. A name
that is a byte-prefix of another is applied first, so
`MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT` wins over `MY_APP__DAEMON` on the keys the longer path
sets.

Decided: A variable whose encoded name starts with the prefix, and whose
name or value is not valid Unicode, returns `ConfigError::NonUnicode` (code
`CFG.NON_UNICODE`) and carries the name as `OsString`. A non-Unicode name
that does not start with the prefix is ignored. The load does not panic and
does not apply a lossy conversion
([NFR-CFG-0001](requirements.md)).

Worked example for app `my-app`. Value after merging the files:

```json
{
  "daemon": { "host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 9000 },
  "logging": { "level": "info", "targets": ["stdout", "file"] }
}
```

Environment:

```text
MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT=8080
MY_APP__DAEMON__HOST=0.0.0.0
MY_APP__DAEMON__TLS=true
MY_APP__DAEMON__MAX_CONNECTIONS=5
MY_APP__LOGGING__LEVEL=debug
MY_APP__LOGGING__TARGETS=["stderr"]
MY_APP__STORES__SQLITE__PATH=data/other.db
MY_APP__LABEL="8080"
OTHER_APP__DAEMON__PORT=1
MY_APP_DAEMON_PORT=2
PATH=/usr/bin
```

Result:

```json
{
  "daemon": {
    "host": "0.0.0.0",
    "port": 8080,
    "tls": true,
    "max_connections": 5
  },
  "logging": { "level": "debug", "targets": ["stderr"] },
  "stores": { "sqlite": { "path": "data/other.db" } },
  "label": "8080"
}
```

`port` is the number `8080` and `label` is the string `"8080"`. `stores` and
`stores.sqlite` did not exist and were created. The last three variables do
not start with `MY_APP__` and are ignored. Adding `MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT__X=1`
to this environment makes the load fail, because `daemon.port` is a number and
cannot be descended into.

statements.text: The prefix MUST be the app name with every ASCII lower-case letter upper-cased and every `-` replaced by `_`, followed by `__` (two underscores).
A variable MUST be treated as an override if and only if its encoded name starts with that prefix.
Every variable whose name does not start with the prefix MUST be ignored, whatever its value.
The part of the name after the prefix MUST be split at every non-overlapping occurrence of `__`, scanning left to right (Rust `str::split("__")`).
Each resulting segment MUST be converted to ASCII lower case.
The variable's value MUST be parsed with `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>`.
If parsing succeeds, the parsed JSON value MUST be used.
If parsing fails, the value MUST be used unchanged as a JSON string.
Starting at the document root, for each of `k1` to `k(n-1)`: if the current value is an object that lacks the key, an empty object MUST be created at that key.

If the current value at any step of that walk, including the root, is not an object (it is a string, number, boolean, array or `null`), the load MUST fail with the `ConfigError` variant for an override that cannot be applied ([REQ-CFG-0004](requirements.md)).
At the last object, key `kn` MUST be set to the override value.
Overrides MUST take precedence over `config/default.json` and `config/local.json`.
A single `_` MUST NOT separate segments.
The document MUST NOT be silently restructured.

requirements.rationale:
Deployments and CI need to change a setting without editing a file, and the
design requires environment-variable overrides for that reason. `__` is the
separator so that a key may itself contain `_`, which snake-case keys do.
Lower-casing the segments lets variables follow the upper-case convention
while JSON keys stay snake case. Parsing the value as JSON lets a number or a
boolean be overridden with the right type, so the caller's `u16` port field
still deserialises; falling back to a string keeps plain values such as paths
and log levels free of quoting. Failing on a path that runs through a
non-object value surfaces a typo or a stale variable instead of reshaping the
document behind the user's back. The design does not state a naming scheme;
this item decides one so that every `sc-config` application is overridden the
same way.

success_criteria.text:
All tests live in `crates/sc-config`, use an in-memory environment and a
temporary config directory ([REQ-CFG-0003](requirements.md)), and do not set
process environment variables.

1. A unit test loads the merged value and the environment of the worked
   example into `serde_json::Value` for app `my-app` and asserts the result
   equals the result shown above.
2. A unit test asserts, one case each, that the values `8080`, `true`, `null`,
   `["a"]` and `{"x":1}` produce a JSON number, boolean, null, array and
   object at the addressed key.
3. A unit test asserts that the values `debug`, `0.0.0.0` and the empty value
   produce the JSON strings `"debug"`, `"0.0.0.0"` and `""`, and that the
   value `"8080"` (with quotes) produces the JSON string `"8080"`.
4. A unit test with file value `{"daemon":{"port":1}}` and only
   `OTHER_APP__DAEMON__PORT=2`, `MY_APP_DAEMON_PORT=3` and
   `my_app__daemon__port=4` set asserts that the result for app `my-app` is
   `{"daemon":{"port":1}}`.
5. A unit test with file value `{}` and `MY_APP__A__B__C=1` asserts the result
   is `{"a":{"b":{"c":1}}}`.
6. A unit test with file value `{"daemon":{"port":7400}}` and
   `MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT__X=1` asserts the result is `Err` with the
   cannot-be-applied variant and that the error names the variable
   `MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT__X`.
7. A unit test with file value `{"daemon":{"host":"h","port":1}}` and
   `MY_APP__DAEMON={"port":2}` asserts the result is `{"daemon":{"port":2}}`
   (replaced, not merged).
8. A unit test for app `my-app` deserialises into a struct with a field
   `port: u16` inside `daemon`, with `MY_APP__DAEMON__PORT=8080` set, and
   asserts `port == 8080`.

requirements.title: `Loader` takes explicit config directory and environment

requirement_statement.text:
This item covers the `Loader` type of the `sc-config` crate
(`crates/sc-config`).

3. It may be built in memory, for example from a `Vec` of pairs.
10. No code in the crate may call `std::env::set_var`,
    `std::env::remove_var` or `std::env::set_current_dir`, in `src/` or in
    tests. Setting the environment or the working directory of a child
    process with `std::process::Command::env` and
    `std::process::Command::current_dir` is allowed, because it does not
    change the state of the test process.
11. No file under `crates/sc-config`, code or tests, may contain a literal temporary-directory path or a literal home-directory path (`/tmp/`, `/home/`, `/Users/`). The repository-wide rule is [NFR-RUN-0005](../requirements.md): non-test code contains no such literal, and every test that writes files uses its own temporary directory. Extending the literal-path ban to this crate's test code is decided in this document.

Using `./config` and the process environment as the defaults of `load` is
decided in this document; the design fixes only the file names
`config/default.json` and `config/local.json`. The call takes
`AppName::new("my-app")`.

Decided: `Loader::new(app: AppName, config_dir: PathBuf, environment: Vec<(OsString, OsString)>) -> Loader`.
The constructor stores those arguments and does not return `Result`.
`Loader::load` and `load` return `Result<T, ConfigError>`. Environment pairs
are `OsString` so a non-Unicode value is reported instead of panicking.

statements.text: The crate MUST export a public type `Loader`.
A `Loader` MUST be given three inputs explicitly by the caller: the app name, the config directory (a filesystem path), and the environment source.
The environment source MUST be an iterator of (variable name, value) pairs supplied by the caller.
`Loader` MUST expose `Loader::load::<T>()` for any `T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned`, returning `Result<T, ConfigError>`.
`Loader::load` MUST read `default.json` and `local.json` from the given config directory and from nowhere else.
`Loader::load` MUST take overrides from the given environment source and from nowhere else.
`Loader::load` MUST apply the same file merge ([REQ-CFG-0001](requirements.md)) and the same override rules ([REQ-CFG-0002](requirements.md)) as the free function `load`.
The free function `load::<T>(app)` MUST be the convenience form.
It MUST behave exactly as a `Loader` given app name `app`, the directory `config` resolved against the current working directory, and the process environment.
When reading the process environment, `load` MUST use `std::env::vars_os`.
Tests MUST obtain their directories from a temporary-directory API.
It MUST NOT read the process environment.
It MUST NOT use `std::env::vars`, which panics when any variable is not valid Unicode.

requirements.rationale:
The process environment and the current working directory are global to the
process. A test that sets a variable or changes directory races with every
other test in the same binary, and Rust's test runner runs tests in parallel
by default. The repository requires every test that touches the filesystem to
use its own temporary directory and to pass when run in parallel
([NFR-RUN-0005](../requirements.md)). Passing the directory and the
environment in explicitly makes that possible for this crate's own tests and
for the tests of any program that uses it.

success_criteria.text:
1. Inspection: `crates/sc-config/src/lib.rs` exports `AppName`, `Loader`,
   `load` and `ConfigError`.
2. A unit test creates two temporary directories with different
   `default.json` content, builds one `Loader` per directory, and asserts each
   returns its own directory's values.
3. A unit test passes an in-memory environment containing `MY_APP__A=1` to a
   `Loader` for app `my-app` over file value `{"a":0}`, without setting any
   process variable, and asserts the result is `{"a":1}`.
4. A unit test passes an empty in-memory environment and asserts the result
   equals the file value.
5. An integration test covers the free function `load` (entries 8 and 9). It
   writes `config/default.json` with content `{"a":0}` under a temporary
   directory `D`. It starts a helper executable with `std::process::Command`,
   with `.current_dir(D)` and `.env("MY_APP__A", "1")`. The helper calls
   `sc_config::load::<serde_json::Value>` for `AppName::new("my-app")` and prints the result as
   JSON on standard output. The test asserts the printed value is `{"a":1}`.
   How the helper executable is built (for example a test-only binary target
   of the crate) is left to the implementation.
6. An integration test covers entry 6. It starts a helper executable the same
   way, with `.env("MY_APP__A", "1")` set on the child. The helper builds a
   `Loader` for app `my-app` over a directory whose `default.json` is
   `{"a":0}`, with an empty in-memory environment, and prints the result. The
   test asserts the printed value is `{"a":0}`: a matching variable in the
   process environment is not read.
7. `cargo test -p sc-config` passes with the default parallel test runner,
   and passes when two such commands run at the same time.
8. `grep -rnE "set_var|remove_var|set_current_dir" crates/sc-config` returns
   no match.
9. `grep -rn "env::vars()" crates/sc-config/src` returns no match.
10. `grep -rnE "/tmp/|/home/|/Users/" crates/sc-config` returns no match: no
    fixed temporary or home path in code or tests (entry 11).

requirements.title: `ConfigError` variants name the file or variable at fault

requirement_statement.text:
This item covers the public error enum `ConfigError` of the `sc-config` crate
(`crates/sc-config`). It is the error type of `load` and of `Loader::load`.

| # | Failure | Data the variant MUST carry |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `default.json` does not exist in the config directory | the full path that was looked for |
| 2 | `default.json` or `local.json` exists but cannot be read (for example permission denied, or the path is a directory) | the file path |
| 3 | a file's content is not valid JSON; this includes content that is not valid UTF-8, because JSON text is UTF-8 | the file path, and the line and column reported by `serde_json::Error::line()` and `column()` |
| 4 | an environment override cannot be applied because its key path passes through a value that is not a JSON object | the full environment variable name |
| 5 | the merged document does not deserialise into the caller's type `T` | the message of the `serde_json::Error`, the paths of the files that were read, and the names of the environment variables that were applied |

7. Failure 5 lists contributing files and variables because the type mismatch
   is found in the merged document, where the origin of a value is no longer
   known.

Decided: The five load failures are `MissingDefault { path }`,
`Read { path, source }` where `source` is `std::io::Error`,
`Parse { path, line, column, message }`, `Override { variable }`, and
`Deserialize { message, files, variables }`. Name construction adds
`InvalidName { name }` with code `APP.INVALID_NAME`. A prefix-matching
non-Unicode environment entry adds `NonUnicode { variable }`. Stable codes
and recovery steps are the error inventory in
[ADR-CFG-0001](architecture.md).

statements.text: `ConfigError` MUST have one distinct variant for each failure in this table. (see table above)
Each variant MUST carry the listed data as typed fields, not only inside a message string.
A `local.json` that exists but cannot be read MUST produce failure 2, not be skipped.
Failure 1 and failure 2 MUST be distinct variants: "file not found" for `default.json` is failure 1, every other I/O error is failure 2.
`ConfigError` MUST implement `std::fmt::Debug`, `std::fmt::Display` and `std::error::Error`.
The `Display` text of every variant MUST contain the file path or the variable name that the variant carries.
The `Display` text of failure 3 MUST contain the line and the column.
The failure 2 variant SHOULD also carry the underlying `std::io::Error` or its `std::io::ErrorKind`.
A missing `local.json` MUST NOT produce an error.

requirements.rationale:
A configuration error is the first failure a new user meets, and in a
generated project `main.rs` prints this error to the terminal and exits before
any logging exists. "Invalid config" with no file or key leaves the user
searching two files and the environment. Naming the file, the position or the
variable turns the message into a fix. Distinct variants with typed fields let
a calling program branch on the failure, for example to print a hint that
`config/default.json` must be run from the project root, without parsing
message text.

success_criteria.text:
All tests live in `crates/sc-config` and use a `Loader` with a temporary
directory and an in-memory environment.

1. A test with an empty config directory asserts `Err` with the failure 1
   variant and that the carried path ends with `default.json`.
2. A test in which `default.json` is a directory (not a file) asserts `Err`
   with the failure 2 variant carrying that path.
3. A test in which `local.json` is a directory asserts `Err` with the failure
   2 variant carrying the `local.json` path.
4. A test with `default.json` content `{"a": 1,\n  "b": }` asserts `Err` with
   the failure 3 variant, the `default.json` path, and line `2`.
5. A test with a valid `default.json` and `local.json` content `{` asserts
   `Err` with the failure 3 variant carrying the `local.json` path. A second
   case with `default.json` containing the bytes `FF FE 00` asserts the
   failure 3 variant carrying the `default.json` path.
6. A test with file value `{"a":1}` and variable `MY_APP__A__B=2` for app
   `my-app` asserts `Err` with the failure 4 variant carrying the name
   `MY_APP__A__B`.
7. A test with file value `{"port":"not-a-number"}`, a `local.json` of `{}`,
   variable `MY_APP__NAME=x`, and target struct `{ port: u16, name: String }`
   asserts `Err` with the failure 5 variant, that the carried file list
   contains both file paths, and that the carried variable list contains
   `MY_APP__NAME`.
8. For each of the five errors produced above, a test asserts that
   `to_string()` contains the carried file path or variable name, and for
   failure 3 the line number.
9. A compile-time test asserts `ConfigError: std::error::Error`, for example
   `fn assert_error<E: std::error::Error>() {}` called with `ConfigError`.

requirements.title: Public API returns `Result<T, ConfigError>`; no panics

requirement_statement.text:
This item binds all code under `crates/sc-config/src`.

The panic rule for the four library crates of this repository is owned by [NFR-RUN-0009](../requirements.md). There is no allowance for a commented exception. Test code is exempt. This item applies that rule to `sc-config` and adds the crate-specific entries 5 and 6.

1. In Rust this is the discriminated union the design calls for: the caller receives either the value or a typed error and must handle both.
2. No public function or method may return `Option` to signal failure, return
   a boxed or opaque error (`Box<dyn Error>`, `anyhow::Error`), or report
   failure by printing or logging.
3. No code path reachable from a public function or method may panic, for any
   input: any app name, any directory path, any file content, any environment
   content including variables that are not valid Unicode.
7. Implementations of standard traits on public types (`Display`, `Debug`,
   `std::error::Error`, `From`) are not "public methods" for entry 1, but
   entries 3, 4 and 5 apply to them.
8. Code inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules and under `crates/sc-config/tests/` is
   exempt from entries 4 and 5.

Decided: Only an operation that can fail returns `Result<T, ConfigError>`.
`Loader::new` stores a validated `AppName` plus the caller's directory and
environment, so it returns `Loader`. `AppName::new` can fail and returns
`Result<AppName, ConfigError>`. [NFR-RUN-0009](../requirements.md) requires
`Result` of operations that can fail.

statements.text: Every public function and public method of `sc-config` that can fail MUST return `Result<T, ConfigError>`, where `ConfigError` is the crate's public typed error enum ([REQ-CFG-0004](requirements.md)).
Where a slice, string, `Vec` or `serde_json::Value` is accessed, the code MUST use `get`, pattern matching or iterators.
It MUST use `std::env::vars_os()`.
That rule is: code reachable from a public function MUST NOT use `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, or panicking `[]` indexing.
Code reachable from a public function MUST NOT use `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, or panicking `[]` indexing ([NFR-RUN-0009](../requirements.md)).
Stricter than the repository rule, decided in this document: code reachable from a public function MUST NOT use `assert!`, `assert_eq!` or `assert_ne!`.
Stricter than the repository rule, decided in this document: non-test code MUST NOT call `std::env::vars()`, which panics on a variable that is not valid Unicode.

requirements.rationale:
The design states this directly for `sc-config`: every method returns a
discriminated union and nothing panics. Configuration is loaded at the top of
`main`, before logging or any error reporting exists. A panic at that point
prints a Rust backtrace to a user whose actual mistake is a typo in a JSON
file, and an agent driving the program gets output it cannot parse. A typed
error lets the generated `main.rs` print one clear line and return an exit
code.

success_criteria.text:
1. `grep -rnE
   "\.unwrap\(\)|\.expect\(|panic!|unreachable!|todo!|unimplemented!|assert(_eq|_ne)?!"
   crates/sc-config/src` prints no line outside `#[cfg(test)]` modules, or
   each remaining match is shown by review to be unreachable from a public
   function. A comment on the line is not grounds for accepting a match.
2. Inspection of every `pub fn` in `crates/sc-config/src` that can fail: the
   return type is `Result<_, ConfigError>`. Standard trait implementations
   are outside this check. `Loader::new` cannot fail and returns `Loader`.
   `AppName::new` can fail and returns `Result<AppName, ConfigError>`.
3. Inspection of code reachable from a public function in
   `crates/sc-config/src` finds no `[` index expression on a slice, string,
   `Vec` or `serde_json::Value`.
4. `grep -rn "env::vars()" crates/sc-config/src` returns no match.
5. A test feeds each of these to a `Loader` and asserts the call returns
   `Err(ConfigError)` and does not panic: an empty `default.json`; a
   `default.json` containing the bytes `FF FE 00`; a `default.json` truncated
   mid-object (`{"a":`); a config directory path that does not exist.
6. A test feeds a `default.json` whose top-level value is an array (`[1,2]`)
   plus override `MY_APP__A=1` for app `my-app` and asserts `Err`, no panic.
7. A test feeds override values `{`, `]`, a 1 MB string of `[` characters, and
   the empty value, and asserts each call returns (`Ok` or `Err`) without
   panicking.
8. `cargo test -p sc-config` reports no test that fails with "panicked".

requirements.title: `sc-config` depends only on `serde` and `serde_json`

requirement_statement.text:
This item binds `crates/sc-config/Cargo.toml`. It is the owner of the list of
third-party crates `sc-config` may depend on. The edges between the crates of
this workspace, the forbidden edges, and the boundary manifest under
`boundaries/sc-config/` that encodes them are owned by
[REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md), which refers to this item for the
third-party list.

4. The forbidden edges of `sc-config` are `sc-observability`,
   `sc-observability-otlp` (the OTel export crate of `sc-observability`),
   `tokio`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command` and `sc-runtime`. The obligation,
   and the `forbidden_edges` entries of the boundary manifest that
   `sc-lint-boundary` checks, are stated in
   [REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md). This item adds only the `cargo tree`
   check in criterion 3.

Decided: `[dev-dependencies]` is empty. Tests create a private directory
under `std::env::temp_dir` and remove it when the test ends. No third test
crate is added.

statements.text: The `[dependencies]` table of `crates/sc-config/Cargo.toml` MUST contain exactly two entries: `serde` and `serde_json`.
The `ConfigError` type MUST be written by hand.
`[dependencies]` MUST NOT contain optional dependencies or target-specific dependency tables that add a third crate.
`thiserror` and `anyhow` MUST NOT be added.

requirements.rationale:
The design lists exactly `serde` and `serde_json` as the dependencies of
`sc-config` and states that `sc-observability` and its OTel export crate stay
independent of `sc-config`.
`sc-config` is the first thing a program calls and is linked into every CLI as
well as every daemon. A configuration crate that pulled in an async runtime or
a logging stack would add compile time and binary size to every small tool
that only wants to read a JSON file, and would make initialisation order
circular: logging is configured from the values this crate loads.

success_criteria.text:
1. Inspection of `crates/sc-config/Cargo.toml`: the `[dependencies]` table has
   the keys `serde` and `serde_json` and no others, and the file has no
   `[target.*.dependencies]` table.
2. `cargo tree -p sc-config -e normal --depth 1` lists `serde` and
   `serde_json` as the only direct dependencies.
3. `cargo tree -p sc-config -e normal --prefix none` prints no line beginning
   with `<name> ` (the crate name followed by a space) for each of these
   names: `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`, `tokio`,
   `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `thiserror`, `anyhow`. The
   match is on the start of the line because the first line of the output
   holds the checkout path, which may itself contain `sc-runtime`.
4. The boundary manifest under `boundaries/sc-config/` and the
   `sc-lint-boundary` run are checked by the criteria of
   [REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md).

requirements.title: `sc-config` API is synchronous in v0.1

requirement_statement.text:
sc-config provides synchronous startup configuration. This phase adds no watcher, reload or change notification; consumers may add async or reload behavior around it without a framework prohibition.

This item binds all code under `crates/sc-config/src` for the first release
(v0.1).

1. A call to `load` or `Loader::load` reads the files, applies the overrides, deserialises, and returns on the calling thread.
7. Automatic reloading, change notification and async interop are out of scope for v0.1.

statements.text: Every public function and method of `sc-config` MUST be synchronous.
If they are built later they SHOULD go into a separate crate, possibly named `sc-config-tokio`, that depends on `sc-config`.
The crate MUST NOT contain an `async fn`, an `.await`, or a public function that returns a `Future`.
The crate MUST NOT watch files for changes.
The crate MUST NOT reload configuration after a load has returned.
The crate MUST NOT offer change notification: no callbacks, channels or subscriptions.
The crate MUST NOT spawn threads or tasks.

requirements.rationale:
The design records automatic reloading, change notification and async interop
as a note for later, possibly as a separate `sc-config-tokio` crate, and
states they are not in the initial plan. Building them now would bring an
async runtime and a file watcher into every program that reads its
configuration once at start-up, which is every current user. A synchronous
function can be called from `main` before a runtime exists and from inside an
async `main` alike.

success_criteria.text:
1. `grep -rnE "async fn|\.await|impl Future|dyn Future" crates/sc-config/src`
   returns no match.
2. `grep -rn "thread::spawn" crates/sc-config/src` returns no match, and
   `grep -nE "tokio|async-std|futures|notify" crates/sc-config/Cargo.toml`
   returns no match.
3. A test calls `Loader::load` from a plain `#[test]` function with no async
   runtime and asserts it returns `Ok`.
4. A test loads, then rewrites `default.json` with a different value, and
   asserts the value returned by the first load is unchanged and that a second
   explicit load returns the new value.

requirements.title: Workspace member

requirement_statement.text:
Phase D sc-cron consumes the single sc-monty implementation and no longer directly depends on monty/monty-types. It retains cron policy and JSON-to/from-value adaptation; hooks receive values rather than JSON strings. sc-sha is permitted for SHA-256 cache keys. No independent Monty compile/session/host/limits/dump/load engine remains here. Existing unit and integration assertions are ported without deletion or weakening. sc-cron-commands consumes the common sc-command read/write helpers after d-9, without server-feature leakage.

`crates/sc-cron` is a workspace member, ported from beads-cache

`crates/sc-cron` at `develop`. For the initial release ADR-RUN-0017 permits

only a temporary normal `sc-command` 0.2.0 Phase C dependency (initial

release 0.1.1) with

`default-features = false` and no features for the canonical port. Canonical

event values remain direct registry `sc-observability-types` imports.

`sc-runtime` does not name it. The generated daemon may name it only as the

optional `cron` dependency selected by the embedding application; default

generated builds do not link it. Here "name" means a Cargo or other manifest

dependency. Documented wiring may reference the crate in comments and schema

descriptions.

The injection API is packaged at workspace version `0.1.1`, with cron the

fifth public library. Registry types use compatible `1.5.0`, unified to exact

1.5.0 by command's temporary pin. Normal cron enables neither command/server

nor command/test-util; test doubles use dev-dependencies only. The current

local facade is removed during implementation before initial publication.

Capability-proven upstream cleanup removes cron -> command and restores the

original no-sibling boundary.

requirements.rationale: An independently packaged scheduler can be embedded without the generated template. Its sc-command dependency supplies the retained observability port, while sc-storage and sc-monty supply shared storage and interpreter behavior.

acceptance_criteria.text: Isolated default/Monty consumers must prove no axum/rmcp/server leakage; workspace feature unification is not that proof.

requirements.title: Normal crontab strings

requirement_statement.text: A schedule uses a normal crontab string of five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week.

requirements.rationale: The beads-cache expression parser refused a five-field string; a normal crontab string is five fields, minute first (ADR-RUN-0013 Context). Owner, 2026-10-25: schedules are cron strings.

acceptance_criteria.text: `*/5 * * * *` means every fifth minute.

requirements.title: Rust, Python, or Monty hook

requirement_statement.text:
All Monty execution calls sc-monty. Retain the existing cron host adapters, capability behavior and unit/integration assertions as thin value-level adapters, not another interpreter host. A schedule supplies Monty or Python source plus JSON data, which the embedding application can enrich in the shared cron.start transform before persistence. cron.start and cron.end use storage_write with policy-checked CronStorage actions; cron.list uses storage_read. Internal scheduler lifecycle operations retain domain transactions because they are not user commands.

sc-cron is a general-purpose scheduler for application-defined jobs. A schedule row names an in-process `Job`, a Python module, or `Monty { source }` under optional feature `monty`. Python and Monty receive the `sc-cron.hook.v1` object with `protocol`, `event`, `schedule`, `payload`, and `deadline`. It has no consumer-specific beads, bd-cache, or ATM field. The crate exposes no HTTP route, MCP tool, or binary. The consumer owns that API and configures schedule limits; sc-cron does not read sc-config.

Monty hosts are application-owned registrations in an immutable `MontyHostRegistry` installed with `Scheduler::with_monty_hosts`. The empty registry registers no application call. `MontyHostHandler: Send + Sync` accepts a `MontyHostCall` containing its validated `MontyHostName`, positional/keyword JSON arguments, schedule name, hook phase, and row deadline and returns `Result<serde_json::Value, CronError>`; matching closures are supported. `MontyHostName::new` validates the identifier and `as_str()` borrows it; registry keys use the same type while registration still accepts strings. Registration rejects invalid identifiers, duplicate names, and reserved `__hook`, `cron_stop`, and `cron_tick` bindings with `InvalidSpec`. Source can invoke registered functions but cannot install or replace handlers. An unregistered name fails with `HOST_UNDEFINED`. Bridge argument conversion and supplied CLI adapter shape rejection fail with `HOST_DENIED`; a custom handler's returned error, including `CronError::InvalidSpec`, records `HOST_CALL_FAILED` after configured-value redaction. Private typed dispatch preserves supplied-adapter errors without parsing custom error prose. The host checks the row deadline before and after a synchronous handler, but cannot preempt arbitrary application code.

Phase B supplies opt-in `sc_compose_run(subcommand, args)` and `atm_run(subcommand, args)` adapters through this same registry. `ScComposeHostConfig` and `AtmHostConfig` select non-empty executable paths (defaults `sc-compose` and `atm`) and working directories (default the daemon directory captured at configuration). Each adapter accepts one command/subcommand string and an optional list of string arguments, with no keyword arguments. It forwards the non-empty command/subcommand followed by those ordered arguments directly as argv, never through a shell. Every command/subcommand is supported; flags including `--root` are forwarded unchanged. Neither adapter forces render arguments or temp-root staging. Scripts choose arguments, not the configured executable or working directory. Both adapters share the existing blocking child driver in `monty_compose`, generalized for argv/cwd, with row deadline, process-group termination, and `MAX_HOOK_OUTPUT_BYTES` per stream. They do not call the async `process::supervise` from the blocking feed thread or introduce a runtime/`block_on` bridge. A completed child returns `{stdout, stderr, exit_code}`, including nonzero exits; script code decides how that result affects its hook. A deadline expiration records `TimedOut`; spawn, decoding, and capture-limit failures record stable host errors. The adapters receive the resolved environment snapshot from ADR-RUN-0016. Neither CLI is required when its adapter is unused. `render_template` is not a product requirement; an internal helper may remain an implementation convenience without becoming a mandatory registered host function.

MVP accepts application-supplied Monty source without signatures, a separate script-approval mechanism, or a consumer option enabling such a mechanism. Capability registration and environment policy are enforced independently. In-process Monty and custom Rust handlers retain stack-overflow, allocator-abort, panic, and non-cooperative deadline risks; they are not an isolation boundary for hostile code.

The stop/tick ordering, generation fencing, retained REPL, interpreter-checkpoint VM limits, and joined shutdown behavior remain as specified by ADR-RUN-0013. Host calls use the production `drive_feed` resume loop; the cfg(test) helper is not a separate production path.

requirements.rationale: Application-supplied hooks and value adapters let the reusable scheduler execute registered application behavior without implementing another interpreter host.

acceptance_criteria.text: Host registry integration tests invoke custom, sc-compose, and ATM functions through one extension interface.
Argument-forwarding tests cover render and non-render subcommands.
MVP execution requires neither signatures nor approval configuration.

requirements.title: Application schedule storage and compiled-session cache

requirement_statement.text: sc-cron owns CronRow for schedules and MontyBlobRow for compiled hook sessions. Generic storage engines contain no cron-specific schema or SQL.

statements.text: CronRow MUST be stored through Storage<CronRow> in the application database, using the application SQLite file by default.
The schedule row MUST preserve canonical hook_environment data with empty default {"dotenv":[],"variables":{}}.
The configured schedule-row limit MUST count enabled and disabled rows.
CronStorage MUST reject a new schedule row at the configured limit with CronError::InvalidSpec.
Each writer MUST use the embedding application's ScheduleLimits.
Schedule writes MUST reject source that sc-monty cannot compile before its first tick.
Compiled sessions MUST be captured immediately after compilation, before any hook runs.
Compiled-session blobs MUST use sc-sha SHA-256 of the exact source plus Monty dump version as their key.
The schedule-row source MUST remain authoritative for matching a cached blob.
Missing, stale, corrupt, unreadable-version or missing-hook cache entries MUST trigger recompilation from source and replacement of the pre-run blob.
Cache rows MUST use sc-cron-owned generic row schemas and migrations.
sc-cron MUST NOT create a separate cron database by default.
sc-cron MUST NOT persist hook run state in compiled-session blobs.
The configuration schema MUST NOT add a separate environment or secret table.
sc-cron MUST NOT migrate unrelated consumer tables.

requirements.rationale: configuration is one SQLite table. Reloading schedules loads every row into memory; an uncapped row count is unsafe when schedules come from operators or configuration, and sc-cron must not depend on `sc-config` (ADR-RUN-0014).

success_criteria.text: The ported cron conformance tests preserve schedule fields and row-limit behavior. Compiled-cache tests cover source/version match, invalid source at submit, pre-run snapshot timing and each cache-miss condition.

implementation_notes.text: The row limit is application configuration rather than stored table state; independent writers with different configured limits do not enforce one another's limits.

requirements.title: One error enum

requirement_statement.text:
Phase C planned amendment: cooperative operation failures remain CronError::Store
with non-exhaustive StoreErrorKind additions Cancelled, DeadlineExceeded and
Indeterminate, and optional typed TransactionOutcome accessor. No second error
enum/channel or raw SQL/provider prose is added. DeadlineExceeded may carry
confirmed committed-late evidence and must not trigger automatic retry;
Indeterminate never asserts rollback/not-persisted. Existing legacy variants,
stable top-level codes and row outcomes remain unchanged. REQ-CRON-0020 and
ADR-RUN-0018 govern the exact admission/persistence report policy.

Fallible library entry points return `CronError`, including both
`process::supervise` and `process::supervise_with_logger`, which return
`Result<Captured, CronError>`. The variants are `BadExpression`, `InvalidSpec`, `AlreadyActive`, `NotFound`, `HookFailed`, `Store`, and `Fenced`, with codes `BAD_EXPRESSION`, `INVALID_SPEC`, `ALREADY_ACTIVE`, `NOT_FOUND`, `HOOK_FAILED`, `STORE_FAILED`, and `FENCED`.

Application-implemented callback protocols retain their documented results.
`EnvironmentReferenceResolver::resolve` returns the value-free
`EnvironmentReferenceError::{Denied, Unavailable}` protocol; sc-cron maps
those failures or a missing reference to fixed `ENV_REFERENCE` outcomes.
Provider prose is never a second public library error channel.

With feature `monty`, a feed may record `RunOutcome::Failed` or `RunOutcome::TimedOut` instead of returning `CronError`. Stable code tokens appear in `Failed` detail strings as `CODE: message; recovery`. [`RunOutcome::failure_parts`](../../crates/sc-cron/src/run_failure.rs) and [`RunFailureParts`](../../crates/sc-cron/src/run_failure.rs) parse that form for agents and UIs. Host-adapter errors remain internal and do not add a public CronError variant. The inventory matches [architecture.md](architecture.md):

| Condition | Code | `RunOutcome` | Operator recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bridge argument conversion or supplied CLI adapter shape rejected before execution | `HOST_DENIED` | `Failed` | Fix the call's JSON conversion or the supplied adapter's documented argument shape. |
| Custom application handler returns an error, including `InvalidSpec` | `HOST_CALL_FAILED` | `Failed` | Fix the application handler; configured environment values are redacted from the recorded detail. |
| CLI executable missing or not runnable | `HOST_SPAWN` | `Failed` | Fix the configured executable path or install the external CLI. |
| CLI output is invalid UTF-8 or exceeds the per-stream cap | `HOST_OUTPUT` | `Failed` | Return bounded UTF-8 stdout and stderr. |
| CLI exits nonzero | — | Script receives result | Inspect `exit_code` and bounded `stderr`; the adapter does not turn an application CLI result into an automatic hook failure. |
| Undefined name | `HOST_UNDEFINED` | `Failed` | Fix hook source; that name is not defined. |
| Monty `OsCall` other than `Getenv` or `GetEnviron` | `HOST_OS` | `Failed` — detail names the operation | Use the configured host registry and Getenv/GetEnviron; other OS operations remain denied. |
| Allowlisted daemon variable is not Unicode or exceeds the value cap | `ENV_PROCESS_INVALID` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Restart the daemon with a bounded UTF-8 value or remove the name from the allowlist. |
| `.env` path outside daemon policy | `ENV_FILE_DENIED` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Authorize the canonical file/root or remove the schedule source. |
| Required `.env` file missing | `ENV_FILE_MISSING` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Restore the absolute file or mark the source optional. |
| `.env` file invalid | `ENV_FILE_INVALID` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Fix the bounded data-file syntax. Shell expansion is not supported. |
| Reference missing or resolver failed | `ENV_REFERENCE` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Configure the daemon resolver and restore the referenced value. |
| Resolved entry-count or encoded-block limit exceeded | `ENV_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT` | `Failed` — value-free detail | Remove variables or reduce values before retrying. |
| Monty raises during the feed | `HOST_RAISED` | `Failed` | The detail is the exception message. |
| `cron_stop` return value is not a valid stop reply | `HOST_REPLY` | `Failed` — detail is `stop check: HOST_REPLY:` then the parse error | Fix hook source; return an object with string `"action"` (`continue`, `disable`, or `delete`) and a non-empty `"reason"` when disabling or deleting. |
| Monty feed task join failed (cancelled blocking-pool task) | `FEED_TASK_FAILED` | `Failed` | Retry the run; if it persists, inspect blocking-pool capacity and hook source. |
| Monty feed task panicked (worker join) | `FEED_JOIN_FAILED` | `Failed` | Fix the panic in the hook or host and retry the schedule. |
| Monty due task panicked or was cancelled | `DUE_JOIN_FAILED` | `Failed` | Retry the schedule; if it persists, inspect the Monty due task and hook source. |
| Monty due path used for a non-Monty hook | `MONTY_RESOLVE` | `Failed` | Run this row on its Rust or Python target, or set `HookTarget::Monty`. |
| `cron_tick` returned a stop action (disable/delete) | `MONTY_TICK` | `Failed` | Return normally from `cron_tick`; disable and delete belong in `cron_stop`. |
| After the CLI returns, host `Instant` exceeds the row budget |  | `TimedOut`, session dropped | Reduce CLI work or raise the row deadline; the VM clock was paused during the host call. |
| Monty feed-time-limit while the VM is executing (not during the host suspend) |  | `TimedOut` | Interpreter checkpoints govern VM execution; host handlers use the row deadline. |

Host-deadline paths record bare `RunOutcome::TimedOut` with no code token in the stored outcome.

requirements.rationale: Every cross-boundary failure exposes stable codes, causes, and recovery/remediation; agents must be able to act on failures without reading source (framework charter). The variant set and codes match the beads-cache crate that sc-cron ports.

acceptance_criteria.text: The public error type in crates/sc-cron is CronError.

requirements.title: Explicit Python and Monty hook environment

requirement_statement.text:
Python and Monty schedule rows share one `HookEnvironment`; existing
constructors default it to empty. A daemon-scoped `HookEnvironmentHost` names
which daemon-process variables may be inherited, authorizes absolute `.env`
files or canonical roots, and supplies an optional reference resolver. The
generated administrator config exposes empty-by-default `allow_process`,
`allow_dotenv_files`, and `allow_dotenv_roots` arrays. Every
host default is empty. The crate never infers or captures an invoking caller's
environment. The generated daemon passes a prebuilt host policy into scheduler
composition so an application-provided resolver is preserved.

Reference resolution receives the schedule name, variable name, opaque
reference, and row deadline. The provider returns only `Denied`, `Unavailable`,
missing, or a value; sc-cron emits no provider prose. Resolution is bounded by
the row deadline, and expiration is `RunOutcome::TimedOut` before hook source
runs.

The schedule environment contains ordered absolute `.env` sources followed
by name-keyed `Set`, `Reference`, or `Clear` operations. One immutable map is
resolved before `cron.stop` and reused for `cron.tick`: allowlisted daemon
values, then files in declaration order, then schedule operations. Explicit
set values are canonical plaintext schedule data. Daemon, file, and reference
values are never persisted. A non-empty environment on a Rust row is invalid;
trusted Rust jobs keep their existing `Job` interface.

Reference locators are non-secret plaintext registry metadata; only their
resolved values remain external. Every intermediate/final map has at most 128
entries, every stored/resolved value is at most 16 KiB, and the encoded final
block is at most 32,000 UTF-8 bytes. Per-source oversize failures and aggregate
`ENV_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT` failures are value-free.

Python starts with exactly the resolved map rather than the daemon's complete
environment. Monty source initialization and hook feeds answer `Getenv` and
`GetEnviron` from the same map with ordinary absent/default behavior; every
other OS call remains denied. Both sc_compose_run and atm_run children receive that map
and do not inherit the daemon environment. sc-cron never mutates the daemon
process environment. Full semantics, limits, file authorization, and the
release-v1 schema baseline are [ADR-RUN-0016](../architecture.md).

Every hook/provider-controlled failure detail or stop reason has each distinct
non-empty resolved value replaced with `[REDACTED_ENV]` before byte capping and
before fixed codes/recovery, outcomes, events, traces, or persisted reasons are
assembled. Stable text, metadata, and the canonical environment configuration
write are exempt; deliberate set values remain plaintext schedule data. Python
output, Monty exception/return text, and both CLI adapters' stdout/stderr are included. Trusted
direct callers may read raw public `HookOutput` fields, but `HookOutput` debug
formatting omits their contents. This exact-value replacement mitigates
accidental propagation; trusted hooks can transform or exfiltrate values and
remain outside an untrusted-code boundary.

requirements.rationale: Owner (ANC-034): "python/monty having consistent settings would be least confusing" (ANC-037): "Never capture or persist inherited host values accidentally" ADR-RUN-0016: environment variables are not uniformly secrets. Durable values such as `ATM_IDENTITY` and `ATM_TEAM` belong with a schedule. API keys may instead be daemon-wide inherited values, explicit schedule values, references resolved by an application secret provider, or values loaded from an authorized absolute `.env` file.

acceptance_criteria.text: The same environment cases produce equivalent Python and Monty results.
An allowed daemon value is delivered and an unlisted value is absent.
Two schedules set distinct identities and clearing removes a prior value.
Ambient canaries are absent from persisted rows without explicit set input.
A consumer resolver supplies a referenced value without persisting the result.
An authorized absolute dotenv file supplies hook values.
A top-level getenv reads the configured snapshot before cron_stop or cron_tick.

requirements.title: Allowed third-party dependencies

requirement_statement.text:
`rusqlite` leaves this list when the schedule store moves to `Storage<CronRow>`; until that code change lands the list below describes the code as it is.

This item owns the third-party crates `sc-cron` may depend on. The `allowed_dependencies` list is the normal dependencies: `async-trait`, `chrono`, `cron`, `getrandom`, `process-wrap`, `rusqlite` (bundled), `sc-observability-types`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `tempfile`, `tokio`, and `tracing`. `sc-lint-boundary` accepts only workspace package names, so `monty` and `monty-types` are not entries in that list. Feature `monty` stays optional and is enforced by the `sc-cron-tree-default` and `sc-cron-tree-monty` cargo-tree gates in `sc-lint.toml`: the default tree has no `monty` edge, and `--features monty` links `monty` and `monty-types` only. `monty-pool`, `monty-fs`, and `monty-runtime` are not allowed. Only the temporary defaults-off command contract edge in ADR-RUN-0017

is allowed; no other workspace crate is allowed.

The tool-crate exclusion in REQ-RUN-0005 applies to sc-cron: sc-compose and ATM crates are forbidden in production dependencies/imports; test and benchmark references are permitted. CLI process invocation does not create a crate dependency.

requirements.rationale: Owner (ANC-031): "sc-compose and atm crates should be blocked from any production release crate.  sc-compose and atm can be referenced for tests i.e. benchmark tests" `monty` runs in-process when the host controls the code; `monty-pool` runs the interpreter in worker subprocesses for untrusted code. The Monty hook target is the trusted case, and a subprocess pool would spend the process spawn the target exists to avoid. A consumer who does not enable `monty` does not link the interpreter.

acceptance_criteria.text: The `sc-cron-tree-default` and `sc-cron-tree-monty` cargo-tree gates in `sc-lint.toml` enforce that feature `monty` stays optional: the default tree has no `monty` edge, and `--features monty` links `monty` and `monty-types` only.

requirements.note: point 4 points here

requirements.title: Environment isolation and redaction

requirement_statement.text:
Environment names use `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. Construction, persistence,
row decode, and execution enforce 256 bytes per name, 16 `.env` sources, 128 entries, 16 KiB per stored/resolved
value, 4 KiB per reference locator/path, a 32,000-byte encoded final block, a
256 KiB canonical document, and a 1 MiB dotenv file. Names,
paths, values, and references are UTF-8 and NUL-free; ASCII case-fold name
collisions are rejected on every platform. An allowlisted non-Unicode daemon
value fails as `ENV_PROCESS_INVALID`. `.env` files are bounded UTF-8 data
files: no interpolation, command substitution, duplicate names, or NUL.
Canonical path authorization follows symlinks before checking an exact
file/root policy; authorization precedes missing classification. Lookup and
enumeration preserve spelling on Unix; Windows runtime keys are uppercased for
both Python and Monty and lookup is case-insensitive, while stored config keeps
the original spelling. Python, sc-compose, and ATM executables are resolved before
child `PATH` is cleared: basenames use daemon launch `PATH`/Windows `PATHEXT`,
absolute paths are retained, and relative paths with components use the
daemon current directory captured when hook/host configuration is built.

Set values, resolved values, file contents, and reference strings are never
copied from those sources into configuration `Debug`, scheduled errors,
recovery text, `RunOutcome`, tracing, canonical events, or persisted stop
reasons. Stable metadata that happens to equal a short value is not rewritten.
`ChildEnv`, `ChildSpec`, and `PythonHook` use value-free custom `Debug` just
like the environment model. Direct `HookOutput` field access is the sole
trusted raw-output exception. Resolution performs
file I/O off the async hot path, holds no store connection or synchronous lock
across await, and calls no `std::env::set_var` or `std::env::remove_var`.

The implemented registry builder uses `register(name, handler)`,
`with_sc_compose(ScComposeHostConfig)`, and `with_atm(AtmHostConfig)`, each
returning `Result<MontyHostRegistry, CronError>`. The generated development
example and custom closure setup are in [monty-generated-example.md](monty-generated-example.md).
The b-16 child environment is explicitly empty; the resolved-snapshot text
above is the b-17 successor contract.

Shared hook environment implementation (B17):

`sc-cron::HookEnvironment` is the validated, canonical schedule policy;
`HookEnvironmentHost` is separately injected daemon authorization. Names use
portable ASCII identifiers and reject ASCII case collisions. Administrator
process-name, exact dotenv-file, and dotenv-root allowlists default empty.
Absolute normalized file paths are authorized after canonicalization, including
nearest-existing-ancestor resolution for missing suffixes. Bounded regular-file
reads run on the blocking pool. The dotenv parser never evaluates shell or
reads ambient values. Application-owned `EnvironmentReferenceResolver` receives
schedule, variable, opaque locator, and row deadline; missing, denied, unavailable
and invalid provider results use fixed value-free `ENV_REFERENCE` diagnostics.

One occurrence resolves daemon → ordered files → Set/Reference/Clear into an
immutable snapshot before stop, then reuses it for tick, Monty initialization,
and both opt-in CLI adapters. Python starts with `ChildEnv::Only`; direct trusted
callers can explicitly choose Inherit. Monty permits only environment OS reads,
including top-level reads, and denies registered application host calls during
initialization. Retained module globals initialize once per generation;
function-time getenv uses the current occurrence. Executables resolve before
child PATH clearing, independently of configured child working directories.
Windows snapshot names are uppercase and getenv lookup ignores case. Rust jobs
retain their application process environment and reject nonempty schedule policy.

Explicit Set values and opaque reference metadata are intentional plaintext
configuration. Resolved process/file/reference values never persist in registry
writes. Runtime details and reasons redact distinct nonempty snapshot values,
longest first, before caps and fixed diagnostic/recovery assembly. Debug exposes
names/kinds/counts only; trusted raw HookOutput fields remain accessible.
Exact replacement mitigates accidental disclosure and does not isolate hostile
source. The complete first-release SQLite schema is version 1 with canonical
`hook_environment` default `{"dotenv":[],"variables":{}}`; semantic schema checks
reject incompatible unreleased development tables without migrating/overwriting.
The library remains general purpose, with open application host registrations,
no signing/approval gates, and no production dependency on sc-compose or ATM.

requirements.rationale: ADR-RUN-0016: the Python hook inherited the complete daemon environment while Monty denied all OS calls. That is an inconsistent capability boundary and has caused difficult identity/team bugs when a daemon starts under one agent and later executes another agent's schedule. The library must support environment choices without silently capturing host values. Owner (ANC-037): "Never capture or persist inherited host values accidentally"

acceptance_criteria.text: Tests make Python, Monty, both CLI adapter, and resolver paths echo canaries and prove redaction, positive delivery, and absence of a non-allowlisted daemon secret.

requirements.title: Public receiver and cooperative owned shutdown

requirement_statement.text:
This target contract is written against `ScheduleStore` and `SqliteScheduleStore`, which PRD-CRON-2 replaces with `Storage<CronRow>`. It has not been re-planned.

The crate exposes the same nominal canonical logging receiver and supporting

values through `sc_cron::observability`; no parallel trait is introduced.

Existing constructors and legacy store implementations remain source compatible.

The open ScheduleStore and generic Scheduler seam permits application-owned

columns/tables through custom stores; bundled-schema preservation does not

forbid consumer schemas or add product fields to Schedule/command DTOs.

Cooperative custom providers must truthfully declare support and forward the

live operation scope, fencing/query semantics and outcome/ownership contract

using their own mechanisms. SQLite-specific callbacks apply to the bundled

SqliteScheduleStore, not to every provider. Legacy/custom integrations may use

the existing caller-owned path with explicitly documented guarantees.

An opt-in cooperative mode rejects unsupported stores before starting work.

It installs one shared operation context before initial load, queue submission,

lock acquisition, reload, decode and all persistence/retry/end paths. Context

checks and provider interruption observe directly mutable

deadlines while blocked. No guard waits indefinitely before consulting context.

Independent stop control closes admission, records only earlier deadlines and

wakes/interrupts operations while an owning join runs. Grace and cleanup are

absolute `std::time::Instant` deadlines in a real stop domain distinct from

the schedule `Clock`. Equal deadlines are valid: T=0 cancels immediately and

grants no cleanup-write budget. Physical joins may take time; no literal

zero-duration or arbitrary native/custom-host preemption guarantee is made.

All admitted worker and context-aware command tasks remain physically owned

until completion even if their async waiter is cancelled. The human-approved

commit admission/outcome contract forbids new ordinary commit admission at/after

G and cleanup commit admission at/after K; it does not promise universal physical

commit/fsync completion by those cutoffs. For bundled SQLite, final commit_hook admission briefly

serializes with live stop state/class/generation/real time, releases the

controller mutex before COMMIT/native I/O, and records stop-first/admission-first.

Second stop remains independently callable while the commit path is blocked.

Explicit and implicit writes share the fence. Confirmed committed-late,

confirmed rollback, no-mutation and indeterminate outcomes are typed distinctly;

expiry/Drop cannot imply rollback or not-persisted. No replay of uncertain

mutations or expired-context readback. Bounded separately authorized readback

may reconcile observed state without claiming exactly-once identity. Uncertain

connection state remains owned/quarantined; restore known hooks/TLS baseline

on safe paths. No effects occur after actual physical release. Cleanup expiry

and actual persisted result are reported honestly after join; no bool false

stands for unknown, no instantaneous T=0 join or universal 2T guarantee.

Legacy direct calls remain

caller-owned. Preserve bundled schema, generation fencing, stop-before-tick, existing

Rust/Python/Monty hooks and REQ-CRON-0019 environment policy.

requirements.rationale: Make the existing cron library consumable through its public logging facade and cooperative operation/lifecycle contract, preserving the already ported Rust, Python and optional Monty execution targets. The framework charter leaves application stores, schemas and wiring to the consumer. Owner (ANC-017): "it is not sc-runtime job to guarantee a customer can not misuse the core libraries."

acceptance_criteria.text: The cron README and isolated external consumer prove one custom field and the chosen cooperative-or-legacy lifecycle through public scheduling/query/end APIs.

implementation_notes.text: Phase C approved target contract (planned, not implemented).

requirements.title: Tracked public operations and bounded schedule query

requirement_statement.text:
The standard Scheduler path has finite shared intake for public context-aware
start/end/query roots: default64, validated pre-start capacity 1..=65536,
immediate fixed typed unavailable refusal before registered/queued work when
full. One permit remains owned through actual physical completion even when
its async waiter is dropped. Stop/deadline/cancellation admission is atomic;
no hidden capacity-wait queue or automatic replay. Worker dispatch and restricted
internal cleanup retain separate existing ownership and cannot serve as a
public-command bypass. This completes REQ-CRON-0020's admission promise under
NFR-RUN-0002 and ADR-RUN-0018; it does not alter embedder row limits or impose
this mechanism on custom CronOperations/CronExecutor policy. The Phase C
contract defines exact configuration, reason mapping and causal proof owners.

The scheduler provides async context-aware start, generation-fenced stop and
query operations using the same tracked admission and cancellation protocol.
They are required by standard command execution; transport timeout cannot detach
a blocking mutation. A bounded query supports active/ended/all selection,
optional name, ascending stable id continuation and a positive capped limit.
It reads the existing table; `list_active` alone cannot satisfy this contract.
A legacy store's new capability defaults to a fixed unsupported error. End by
name resolves a specific id/generation and cannot end a replacement generation.
The public object-safe native CronOperations port returns boxed Result futures
for start/end/query with StoreOperationContext; it carries no adapter DTOs.
Scheduler's real implementation belongs to c-5. with_deadline derives a child
sharing stop/admission state and the earliest deadline; no independent registry.
No new job kind, job registry, second database or arbitrary hard-delete command
is implied. Ordinary registration continues through REQ-CRON-0003 APIs.

C1 application-owned control construction:

The ordinary-feature `WorkerStopControl::new()` factory creates a live
operation scope inside its owning Tokio runtime, without a Scheduler,
framework worker or test-utils. Applications implementing CronOperations own
intake, physical work and joins. After requesting stop and physically joining
that work, `finish_application_shutdown()` acknowledges completion and
revokes existing and newly obtained scopes even when G was in the future.
The runtime must remain alive for independent status notifications. A checked
ShutdownBudget has private fields and read-only grace()/cleanup() accessors;
K cannot precede G. Existing framework workers retain WorkerHandle-owned joins.

requirements.rationale: This completes the existing pre-submission admission/physical-ownership promise of REQ-CRON-0020/0021 and ADR-RUN-0018 under NFR-RUN-0002's nonblocking request path and the existing service-hardening production checklist section 7.

acceptance_criteria.text: Real query returns ended as well as active rows with deterministic bounded continuation; malformed limits/cursors fail; replacement races preserve generation fencing.
Cancellation of command waiters leaves no untracked work.

implementation_notes.text: Phase C approved target contract (planned, not implemented).

requirements.title: One standard versioned cron command contract

requirement_statement.text:
Provide `cron.start`, `cron.end` and `cron.list` through strict version-1 JSON
DTOs and existing sc-command Envelope/OpError. CLI, REST and MCP projections
use the same request, typed result and namespaced error codes. Start selects
existing Rust, Python or optional Monty targets, ordinary five-field cron or
supported aliases, bounded timeout and opaque payload/environment. Rust uses
the application-configured Job/dispatcher; no serialized function or new job
catalog. End requires name and generation. List supports bounded deterministic
active/ended/all continuation with id/generation/state views. No implicit
end-all, hard deletion, ATM team/phase/mandatory-until or six-field-only grammar.

Reject unknown/duplicate fields, invalid version/generation/limits/cursor,
overflow and unsupported target before writes. Freeze exact core-derived size
limits and value-free error mapping in the contract sprint. Do not expose raw
SQL, environment values, source code or payload in diagnostics. Read views
exclude sensitive source/environment/payload unless a separate authorized
application projection explicitly exposes them.

requirements.rationale: This optional library reconciles the new human command requirement with the scheduler core's existing no-product-API rule.

acceptance_criteria.text: Serialization/schema tests demonstrate one canonical versioned start/end/list and Envelope result/error across projection-neutral fixtures.
All invalid forms fail before scheduler/store work; no absent name means end-all.

implementation_notes.text: Phase C target, planned and unimplemented.

requirements.title: Optional executor and actual opt-in UI wiring

requirement_statement.text:
Default-surface object-safe CronExecutor accepts sole CronRequest and real
deadline. Scheduler-feature StandardCronExecutor consumes native CronOperations
and explicit ApplicationTargetBindings ports defined in the Phase C contract;
it derives a child operation context, never a separate timeout/ownership policy
inside the standard executor. Applications may implement CronOperations or
CronExecutor through these public seams for different behavior or shutdown
policy; their task/physical-join ownership, persistence truth, authorization
