requirements.title: Endpoint resolution order in `sc-transport`

requirement_statement.text:
In the crate's public-surface sketch these are `Endpoint::Uds(PathBuf)` and `Endpoint::Tcp(SocketAddr)`, produced by `resolve_endpoint(...)`.

This precedence order is decided in this document; the sc-runtime design lists the sources (`--endpoint`, `SC_ENDPOINT`, config, platform default) but not their order.

| Order | Source | How the value reaches the resolver |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the `--endpoint` command-line flag | The calling binary parses the flag (the crate MUST NOT depend on `clap` or parse `argv`) and passes the value, or "absent", as an argument. |
| 2 | the `SC_ENDPOINT` environment variable | The value of the process environment variable named exactly `SC_ENDPOINT`, passed to the resolver as an explicit argument (the value, or "absent"). |
| 3 | the endpoint from the caller's configuration | The caller passes it as an argument. The crate MUST NOT depend on `sc-config`. |
| 4 | the platform default | Computed by the crate, see below. |

The crate MAY also offer a convenience form of the resolver that reads the variable itself. Both points are decided in this document; the sc-runtime design names `SC_ENDPOINT` as a source but does not say who reads it.

| Platform | Default endpoint |
|---|---|
| macOS and Linux | UDS at `<instance-root>/daemon.sock` |
| Windows | TCP on IP address `127.0.0.1`, with the port taken from the caller's configuration |

`<instance-root>` is the per-application, per-user directory resolved by
sc-transport, or an explicitly supplied path. On Unix the default base is
non-empty `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, otherwise `$HOME/.local/state`. On Windows it
is `LOCALAPPDATA`. The path is `<base>/<app>`
([REQ-TRN-0002](requirements.md)). `instance_root` does not create it.

The Windows address `127.0.0.1` is stated by the sc-runtime design. That the Windows port comes from the caller's configuration is decided in this document: the design states "port from config" for cross-host TCP and names no port for the Windows default.

`DaemonConfig` embeds this type ([REQ-RT-0001](../sc-runtime/requirements.md), [REQ-RT-0008](../sc-runtime/requirements.md)); a CLI's configuration uses it directly. The resolver takes source 3 and the explicit instance root from a value of this type or from its fields.

Any code that needs that string, including `sc_runtime::testing::DaemonFixture` ([REQ-RT-0006](../sc-runtime/requirements.md)), obtains it from this conversion and does not format it itself. This follows from REQ-RT-0006 and [REQ-RT-0008](../sc-runtime/requirements.md), which bar `sc-runtime` from holding endpoint logic. The conversion is `Display` and `FromStr` on `Endpoint`: `uds:<path>` and `tcp:<socket-addr>`. `tcp:` takes a literal `SocketAddr` and does not resolve DNS. An empty string is `TransportError::InvalidEndpoint` and does not fall through.

Pinned by sprint a-3:

- The endpoint type is `Endpoint::{Uds(PathBuf), Tcp(SocketAddr)}`.
- The resolver is
  `resolve_endpoint(&AppName, flag: Option<&OsStr>, environment: Option<&OsStr>, &TransportConfig) -> Result<Endpoint, TransportError>`.
  `resolve_endpoint_from_env` is the convenience form and reads only
  `std::env::var_os("SC_ENDPOINT")`.
- An unparseable value is `TransportError::InvalidEndpoint`
  (`TRANSPORT.INVALID_ENDPOINT`).
- The configuration type is `TransportConfig`. It is `#[non_exhaustive]`
  and `serde::Deserialize`. Its fields are `endpoint: Option<String>`,
  `instance_root: Option<PathBuf>`, and `tcp_port: Option<u16>`. It has no
  `additional_endpoints` field. v0.1 binds exactly one listener per config.
  A later dual-bind adds a field on this type. v0.1 does not ignore a
  reserved value. `DaemonConfig` field names stay with
  [REQ-RT-0001](../sc-runtime/requirements.md); that type embeds
  `TransportConfig`.
- On Windows, a missing `tcp_port` with no override is
  `TransportError::MissingTcpPort` (`TRANSPORT.MISSING_TCP_PORT`). `detail`
  says to set `TransportConfig.tcp_port` or pass a `tcp:` override. This
  crate has no default TCP port.
- An override or `TransportConfig.endpoint` that names `uds:<path>` is a
  UDS endpoint on every platform, including Windows. The resolver returns
  it. `Client::new` and `bind` reject a UDS endpoint on non-Unix targets
  when they are used (`TransportError::Request` and
  `TransportError::UnsupportedEndpoint`).

Whether the project template writes a default TCP port into generated
configuration stays with [REQ-RUN-0301](../requirements.md). This crate does
not decide that.

statements.text: The crate `sc-transport` (`crates/sc-transport`) MUST expose one public endpoint resolver that both a daemon binary and a CLI binary call to learn where the daemon listens.
The resolver's result MUST be one of exactly two cases: a Unix domain socket (UDS) path, or a TCP socket address.
The resolver MUST pick the first source below that supplies a value. (see table above)
The resolver MUST accept the `SC_ENDPOINT` value as an explicit input, so that a caller or a test can supply it without changing the process environment.
That form MUST read it with `std::env::var_os("SC_ENDPOINT")`, MUST NOT use `std::env::var` or `std::env::vars`, and MUST then call the explicit-input form.
The platform default MUST be: (see table above)
The endpoint and instance-root portion of a project's configuration MUST be one public type exported by `sc-transport` with default features, and that type MUST implement `serde::Deserialize`.
A source value that cannot be parsed as an endpoint MUST produce an `Err` of the crate's error enum `TransportError`.
The crate MUST also provide, with default features, the reverse conversion: from a resolved endpoint to the string form accepted by `--endpoint` and `SC_ENDPOINT`.
Parsing the rendered string MUST yield an endpoint equal to the original.
The crate MUST NOT contain a literal TCP port number that it uses as a default; TCP ports come only from an override or from the caller's configuration ([ADR-TRN-0002](architecture.md)).

This follows from two other binding facts: the CLI and the daemon must give the resolver the same configuration value, and a CLI MUST NOT depend on `sc-runtime`, so it cannot name `sc_runtime::DaemonConfig`.
The resolver MUST NOT panic and MUST NOT silently fall through to the next source in that case.

requirements.rationale:
A daemon and its CLI are separate binaries with no run-time coordination. If
they compute the endpoint differently they never meet, so one resolver used
by both makes disagreement impossible. UDS is the default on macOS and Linux
because access is controlled by file permissions and it needs no port and no
token, the same approach dockerd uses. Windows defaults to TCP because
reqwest's `ClientBuilder::unix_socket` exists only on Unix. Cross-host use
and browser frontends use TCP with a port from configuration; port ranges are
registered centrally in the synaptic-canvas repository. The override sources
exist so tests and multi-instance setups can point both binaries somewhere
else. `SC_ENDPOINT` is an explicit input because tests run in parallel in one
process, and a test that sets a process-wide environment variable breaks the
others. The configuration type lives here because this is the only crate
that both a CLI and a daemon depend on for endpoints. The callers are the
generated `cli` and `daemon`, which each accept `--endpoint`
([REQ-RUN-0310](../requirements.md)), and `sc-runtime`'s `run()`, which
resolves the daemon's bind endpoint only through this resolver
([REQ-RT-0008](../sc-runtime/requirements.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. A unit test in `crates/sc-transport` supplies all of sources 1, 2 and 3
   with three different valid endpoints and asserts the result equals the
   source 1 value.
2. A unit test supplies sources 2 and 3 only, both as explicit arguments,
   and asserts the result equals the supplied `SC_ENDPOINT` value.
3. A unit test supplies source 3 only and asserts the result equals the
   configuration value.
4. A unit test compiled only on Unix (`#[cfg(unix)]`) supplies no source,
   uses an explicit instance root `R` (a tempdir), and asserts the result is
   the UDS path `R/daemon.sock`.
5. A unit test compiled only on Windows (`#[cfg(windows)]`) supplies no
   override and a configuration port `P`, and asserts the result is the TCP
   address `127.0.0.1:P`.
6. A unit test supplies an unparseable source 1 value and asserts the result
   is `Err` with `TransportError::InvalidEndpoint`. The source 2 value is
   not returned.
7. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport` (source and tests) finds no call to
   `std::env::set_var` or `std::env::remove_var`; tests 1 to 6 pass
   `SC_ENDPOINT` as an argument and pass under the default parallel test
   runner.
8. `crates/sc-transport/Cargo.toml` lists neither `clap` nor `sc-config`.
9. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/src` finds that the string
   `SC_ENDPOINT` is read, if at all, only through `std::env::var_os`, and
   finds no call to `std::env::var(` or `std::env::vars`.
10. `cargo doc -p sc-transport` with default features lists the public
    configuration type, and a test containing
    `fn assert_de<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>() {}` instantiated with
    that type compiles.
11. Inspection of non-test code in `crates/sc-transport/src` finds no
    literal TCP port number used as a default endpoint.
12. A unit test renders one UDS endpoint and one TCP endpoint to the string
    form, parses each string back as an explicit `--endpoint` value, and
    asserts the result equals the original endpoint, and asserts the literal
    strings `uds:<path>` and `tcp:<socket-addr>`.

requirements.title: Instance root directory resolution in `sc-transport`

requirement_statement.text:
The instance root is the one directory that holds a daemon's run-time files
for one application and one operating-system user: the UDS socket file
`daemon.sock` and the singleton lock file `daemon.lock`.

The function is `instance_root(&AppName) -> Result<PathBuf, TransportError>`. The crate-private function `instance_root_from_base(&AppName, Option<&Path>)` is the path builder that receives the per-user base. It is not a facade item.

The public function obtains the base location from the operating system or environment and calls that function. This structure is decided in this document.

The default base is decided by sprint a-3:

- Unix: non-empty `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, otherwise `$HOME/.local/state`.
- Windows: non-empty `LOCALAPPDATA`.
- The instance root is `<base>/<app>`. `instance_root` does not create the
  directory. The caller creates it.
- An explicit `TransportConfig.instance_root` is used unchanged as the Unix
  default's directory (`<explicit>/daemon.sock`), not as `<explicit>/<app>`.
- Failure is `TransportError::InstanceRootUnavailable`
  (`TRANSPORT.INSTANCE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE`).

`AppName::new` accepts ASCII `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, and `_`, length
1 through 64 bytes. Rejection is `TransportError::InvalidName`
(`APP.INVALID_NAME`). `detail` says whether the name was empty, longer than
64 bytes, or which character was outside that set. The type exposes `as_str`
and `AsRef<str>`. It does not implement `Deref`. Tests load
`tests/fixtures/app-name-vectors.json` and do not embed a second list.

statements.text: The crate `sc-transport` MUST expose a public function that takes an application name (an [`AppName`](architecture.md), such as `"my-app"`) and returns the default instance root path for that application and the current user.
The default instance root MUST be a per-user location: two different operating-system users MUST get different paths for the same application name.
Two different application names MUST give different paths for the same user.
The same application name and user MUST give the same path on every call.
The function MUST compute the path at run time from the operating system or environment.

Every public function of the crate that uses an instance root (endpoint resolution in particular) MUST also accept an explicitly supplied instance root path, and MUST use that path unchanged in place of the default when it is supplied.
Failure to determine the default location MUST be returned as an `Err` of the crate's error enum `TransportError`.

The default path MUST be built by one function inside the crate that receives the per-user base location as an input (a path, or "absent"), so that the per-user property and the failure case can be tested without changing the process environment.
The source MUST NOT contain a literal home-directory or temp-directory path such as `/tmp` or `/Users/...`.
The function MUST NOT panic.

requirements.rationale:
The socket and the daemon lock live in the instance root, so the directory
is what identifies "this application's daemon for this user". Daemon and CLI
must derive it the same way or the CLI looks for the socket in the wrong
place. The explicit override exists for tests: every test that touches the
filesystem or starts a daemon must use its own tempdir as instance root so
that tests run in parallel and never touch a developer's real daemon
([NFR-RUN-0005](../requirements.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. A unit test calls the default resolution twice with the application name
   `"app-a"` and asserts both results are equal.
2. A unit test calls the default resolution with `"app-a"` and `"app-b"` and
   asserts the two paths differ.
3. A unit test supplies an explicit instance root `R` (a tempdir) and asserts
   that endpoint resolution with no other source returns `R/daemon.sock` on
   Unix, that is, `R` is used unchanged and the default is not consulted.
4. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/src` finds no string literal that
   starts with `/tmp`, `/home`, `/Users` or `C:\`.
5. No test in `crates/sc-transport` creates a file under the default
   instance root; every test that writes files uses a tempdir.
6. A unit test calls the path-building function with the application name
   `"app-a"` and two different per-user base locations `B1` and `B2` (two
   tempdirs) and asserts the two results differ, the first starts with `B1`
   and the second starts with `B2`.
7. A unit test calls the path-building function with the base location
   absent and asserts the result is `Err` with a `TransportError`, with no
   panic.
8. Inspection of `instance_root` finds that the base location is
   `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` or `HOME` on Unix and `LOCALAPPDATA` on Windows, read
   at run time with `std::env::var_os`.

requirements.title: UDS and TCP listener binding behind the `server` feature

requirement_statement.text:
In the crate's public-surface sketch these are `bind(&Endpoint) -> Result<Listener, TransportError>` and `Listener`. `Listener` is one type for both transports. `local_endpoint` returns the bound `Endpoint` (`TransportError::Bind` if the TCP address cannot be read). A TCP port of `0` is reported as the port the operating system assigned. `Listener` implements `axum::serve::Listener`.

It has no `additional_endpoints` field. A later dual-bind adds a field on that type. v0.1 does not ignore a reserved value. Calling `bind` twice remains valid. Whether `sc_runtime::Daemon::builder()` uses two listeners is owned by [REQ-RT-0001](../sc-runtime/requirements.md); a-5 copies the one-listener decision into the root documents. This crate's dual-bind question is closed.

A bind failure is `TransportError::Bind` (`TRANSPORT.BIND`). The endpoint
lock already being held is `TransportError::EndpointBusy`
(`TRANSPORT.ENDPOINT_BUSY`). On a non-Unix target, `bind` of a UDS endpoint
returns `TransportError::UnsupportedEndpoint`
(`TRANSPORT.UNSUPPORTED_ENDPOINT`). Recovery tells the caller to use a
`tcp:` endpoint. The parent directory is not created.

statements.text: When the cargo feature `server` of the crate `sc-transport` is enabled, the crate MUST expose a public function that takes a resolved endpoint (a UDS path or a TCP socket address) and returns a bound listener.
The returned listener MUST be accepted by `axum::serve` (axum 0.8) together with an ordinary `axum::Router`.
For a UDS endpoint the function MUST bind a Unix domain socket at the given path.
For a TCP endpoint the function MUST bind the given socket address.
When the TCP port is `0` the listener MUST let the caller read the actual bound address.
One process MUST be able to hold a UDS listener and a TCP listener from this same time and serve the same router on both. v0.1 `TransportConfig` describes exactly one endpoint.
A bind failure (for example the address is in use, or the directory does not exist) MUST be returned as an `Err` of the crate's error enum `TransportError`.
The router and its handlers MUST NOT need any change, type parameter or wrapper that depends on whether the listener is UDS or TCP.
The function MUST NOT panic.
The function and the listener type MUST NOT exist in a build without the `server` feature.

requirements.rationale:
`axum::serve` accepts a `tokio::net::TcpListener` or a
`tokio::net::UnixListener` with no change to routes, so the transport is a
configuration choice that route code never sees. Binding both at once serves
the case where a browser frontend needs TCP while the CLI stays on the
socket. The code is behind `server` because it needs axum, and a CLI that
uses this crate must not link axum.

success_criteria.text:
1. A test compiled with `--features server` on Unix binds a UDS endpoint in
   a tempdir, serves a router with one `GET` route through `axum::serve`,
   requests that route over the socket, and asserts status 200 and the
   expected body.
2. A test compiled with `--features server` binds the TCP endpoint
   `127.0.0.1:0`, reads the bound address, serves the same router function,
   requests the route over TCP, and asserts status 200 and the expected
   body.
3. A test compiled with `--features server` on Unix binds one UDS and one
   TCP listener in the same process, serves the same router on both, and
   asserts the route answers on both.
4. The router-building function used by tests 1 to 3 is one function with no
   generic parameter or argument that names the transport.
5. A test binds a TCP address that is already bound and asserts the result
   is `Err` with a `TransportError`.
6. `cargo doc -p sc-transport` without the feature shows neither the bind
   function nor the listener type.

requirements.title: UDS socket file permissions and stale-file replacement

requirement_statement.text:
This requirement applies to the listener-binding function of the crate
`sc-transport` (sketched as `bind(&Endpoint)`, behind the `server` cargo
feature) when the endpoint is a UDS path.

1. These permissions are the only access control on a UDS listener ([ADR-TRN-0005](architecture.md)).
2. The lock path is formed by appending the literal `.lock` to the full socket path, not by replacing its extension.
4. This endpoint lock is distinct from `<instance-root>/daemon.lock`: the runtime lock serializes one application instance before stores open, while the endpoint lock protects an arbitrary overridden UDS path shared by otherwise different instance roots. The endpoint-lock file is never deleted; releasing the OS lock is sufficient and avoids a remove/recreate inode race.

Points 2, 3 and 4 are decided in this document
([ADR-TRN-0006](architecture.md)); the sc-runtime design states only that
file permissions restrict access to the user.

`<instance-root>` is the per-application, per-user directory resolved by
sc-transport, or an explicitly supplied path. On Unix the default base is
non-empty `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, otherwise `$HOME/.local/state`. On Windows it
is `LOCALAPPDATA`. The path is `<base>/<app>`
([REQ-TRN-0002](requirements.md)). `instance_root` does not create it.

Removing the old file and setting the permissions happen once, at bind time.
They are outside the request path, so they do not conflict with the rule
that request handling never blocks ([NFR-RUN-0002](../requirements.md)).

The socket file mode is `0o600`. The mode is set on the socket file only.
The instance-root directory is left unchanged. When the existing path is not
a socket, `bind` returns `TransportError::NotASocket`
(`TRANSPORT.NOT_A_SOCKET`) and leaves the path in place.

statements.text: After a successful bind the socket file MUST be accessible only to the operating-system user that owns the process: the file's permission bits for group and for others MUST all be zero (`mode & 0o077 == 0`).
Before inspecting or removing an existing UDS socket file, `bind` MUST acquire a nonblocking OS-exclusive endpoint lock at the sibling path `<socket-path>.lock`.
The returned `Listener` MUST retain that lock for its lifetime.
Once it holds the endpoint lock, `bind` MUST remove an existing stale socket file and bind the new socket at the same path.
Cleanup MUST remove the socket only while the same `Listener` still holds the endpoint lock.
Failure to acquire it is a typed bind error and MUST NOT inspect, remove, or replace the socket file.
It MUST NOT fail with "address in use" merely because a socket file was left by a process that no longer holds the endpoint lock.
It MUST NOT use a connect probe or process check to infer liveness.
A failed competing bind or its cleanup MUST NOT remove another listener's socket.

requirements.rationale:
File permissions are the only access control on the default transport, so a
socket that other users can open would expose the daemon to them. A leftover
socket file would make every restart after a crash fail with "address in
use". Replacing it is safe only after acquiring ownership scoped to the
endpoint itself. An instance-root lock is insufficient because two distinct
instance roots may resolve to the same overridden socket path.

success_criteria.text:
1. A test (`#[cfg(unix)]`, `--features server`) binds a UDS endpoint in a
   tempdir, reads the socket file's metadata, and asserts
   `mode & 0o077 == 0`.
2. A test (`#[cfg(unix)]`, `--features server`) creates a stale socket file
   by binding a `std::os::unix::net::UnixListener` at a tempdir path and
   dropping it without removing the file, then calls the crate's bind on the
   same path and asserts `Ok`.
3. The same test then serves a router on the new listener and asserts a
   request over the socket gets status 200.
4. A first listener binds a UDS path. A second bind of that same path fails
   without unlinking it; a request still reaches the first listener. Dropping
   the failed result cannot remove the first listener's socket.
5. `cargo doc -p sc-transport --features server` states the endpoint-lock
   path, retention lifetime, stale-file replacement, and cleanup rule.
6. Inspection finds no connect probe or process check before stale-file
   removal, and proves the endpoint lock is acquired first and retained by
   `Listener`; no path deletes the endpoint-lock file.

requirements.title: Typed HTTP client `Client` built on reqwest

requirement_statement.text:
In the design sketch it is used as:

```rust
let client = sc_transport::Client::new(endpoint)?;
let widget: Envelope<Widget> =
    client.post("/ops/widget.create", &CreateWidget { name }).await?;
```

1. It does not take an application name. `DaemonNotRunning` carries no suggested action ([REQ-TRN-0006](requirements.md)). The endpoint argument is the value returned by the endpoint resolver of [REQ-TRN-0001](requirements.md).
2. The UDS base URL is `http://localhost`.
5. Deserialisation runs for every HTTP status, including non-2xx. A body that is `T` is `Ok(T)`.
7. No method may panic; every failure is a `TransportError` value.

The constructor signature is
`Client::new(endpoint: Endpoint) -> Result<Client, TransportError>`.
It stores the endpoint and builds the reqwest client. It does not contact
the daemon. An unreachable daemon is first reported by `get` or `post`.
Connect timeout and request timeout are each two seconds. The caller cannot
set them in v0.1. [ADR-TRN-0001](architecture.md) reserves a future
`#[non_exhaustive] ClientOptions` and `Client::with_options` for timeouts
and default headers. v0.1 does not define that type. `Client::new` stays the
handoff constructor. On a non-Unix target, `Client::new` with a UDS endpoint
returns `TransportError::Request`. The resolver may still return that UDS
endpoint.

statements.text: The crate `sc-transport` MUST expose, in its default build (no cargo features), a public HTTP client type.
`Client::new(endpoint)` MUST take an endpoint (a UDS path or a TCP address) and nothing else.
It MUST build a `reqwest::Client` (reqwest 0.13).
For a UDS endpoint it MUST configure it with `reqwest::ClientBuilder::unix_socket(path)`.
For a TCP endpoint it MUST use the base URL `http://<ip>:<port>`.
`get(path)` MUST send an HTTP `GET` to `path` on that endpoint.
`post(path, &body)` MUST send an HTTP `POST` to `path` with `body` serialised as JSON, for any `B: serde::Serialize`.
Both methods MUST be `async`, MUST deserialise the JSON response body into the caller-chosen type `T`, for any `T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned`, and MUST return `Result<T, TransportError>`.
`Client::new` MUST NOT perform any endpoint resolution of its own: it MUST NOT read `SC_ENDPOINT`, configuration or the instance root.
The crate MUST NOT name or depend on any concrete response type such as `Envelope<T>`; the caller chooses `T`.

requirements.rationale:
This is the whole client a CLI needs: one constructor call and one call per
operation. Building on `reqwest` gives one well-known HTTP client for both
transports with no extra crate. Being generic over `T` keeps `sc-transport`
free of any dependency on `sc-command`, where the response envelope lives;
the two crates must stay independent so either can be used alone
([ADR-TRN-0003](architecture.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. A test on Unix starts an HTTP server on a UDS path in a tempdir with a
   `POST` route that echoes a JSON struct, calls `Client::new` with that
   endpoint, calls `post` with a test struct
   `Req { name: String }`, and asserts the
   returned test struct `Resp` has the expected field values.
2. The same test over TCP on `127.0.0.1` with an ephemeral port.
3. A test calls `get` on a route that returns a fixed JSON document and
   asserts the deserialised value, over UDS and over TCP.
4. A test calls `get::<Resp>` on a route that returns the body `not json`
   and asserts an `Err` whose variant is not `DaemonNotRunning`.
5. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/src` finds a call to
   `ClientBuilder::unix_socket` and no mention of `Envelope` or `OpError`.
6. The client compiles with default features: `cargo build -p sc-transport`
   (no `--features`) succeeds, and `cargo doc -p sc-transport` for that
   build lists the client type with its `new`, `get` and `post` methods.

requirements.title: Typed error `DaemonNotRunning` (`DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`)

requirement_statement.text:
2. `code()` returns `DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`. The variant has no `suggested_action`, no `AppName`, no `sc_observability_types::ErrorCode`, and no `Remediation`. This crate does not name `daemon start`. a-6 maps the string to `ErrorCode` and owns `suggested_action` for every `TransportError`.
3. Phase A's generated CLI is report-only. Deferred [REQ-RUN-0206](../requirements.md) preserves a possible later optional auto-start layer outside this transport boundary.
4. A body that deserialises as `T` is `Ok(T)` for every HTTP status.
5. Connect timeout and request timeout are each two seconds and are not
   caller-configurable in v0.1. The extension point is `ClientOptions` in
   [ADR-TRN-0001](architecture.md). A timeout is `TransportError::TimedOut`
   (`TRANSPORT.TIMED_OUT`).
6. A client failure that is neither a missing socket, nor connection
   refused, nor a timeout, nor a decode failure is `TransportError::Request`
   (`TRANSPORT.REQUEST`). A UDS path that is a directory is `Request`.

The inventory of every `TransportError` variant is the error-inventory
table in [ADR-TRN-0001](architecture.md). [ADR-TRN-0003](architecture.md)
records the same table as the decision for `DaemonNotRunning`.

statements.text: The error enum `TransportError` of the crate `sc-transport` MUST have a variant `DaemonNotRunning`.

The client ([REQ-TRN-0005](requirements.md): `Client::new`, `get`, `post`) MUST return `TransportError::DaemonNotRunning` from the first `get` or `post` when it cannot open a connection to the endpoint for one of these reasons: the UDS socket file does not exist; the UDS socket file exists but nothing is listening (connection refused); the TCP connection is refused.
`DaemonNotRunning` MUST carry `code: &'static str`, exactly `DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`, the endpoint, and the cause.

A response body that cannot be deserialised into the requested type MUST produce `TransportError::ResponseDecode` (`TRANSPORT.RESPONSE_DECODE`), which carries the HTTP status, the cause, and `body_preview` (a lossy UTF-8 prefix of at most 512 bytes of the body).
The `Client` MUST NOT start the daemon, spawn any process, or retry in order to wait for a daemon.

requirements.rationale:
The daemon being down is the most common CLI failure. It must be told apart
from every other failure so that an agent or a person can branch on the
stable code `DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`. The `Client` only reports; any later
optional auto-start layer under deferred
[REQ-RUN-0206](../requirements.md) would act outside this boundary. The
code is a `&'static str` because this crate must not depend on
`sc-observability-types` or on `sc-command`, where `ErrorCode` and `OpError`
live. a-6 maps the string and chooses `suggested_action`, including any
`daemon start` text. Which envelope a CLI prints for the other
`TransportError` variants is recorded in
[REQ-RUN-0202](../requirements.md).

success_criteria.text:
1. A test on Unix constructs the client against a UDS path in a tempdir where
   no file exists and asserts the first `Err` returned by `get` is
   `TransportError::DaemonNotRunning`.
2. A test on Unix does the same against a stale socket file (a listener
   bound and dropped without removing the file) and asserts
   `DaemonNotRunning`.
3. A test binds `127.0.0.1:0`, records the port, closes the listener, calls
   the client against that port, and asserts `DaemonNotRunning`.
4. Each of tests 1 to 3 asserts the code equals `DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`, the
   endpoint equals the endpoint passed to `Client::new`, and the cause is
   present. The matched fields are `code`, `endpoint`, and `cause`.
5. A same-crate unit test matches `DaemonNotRunning` exhaustively on
   `code`, `endpoint`, and `cause`. The error carries no application name.
   `Client::new` takes an `Endpoint` only.
6. A test asserts that an undecodable response body gives
   `ResponseDecode` whose `body_preview` contains that body, and that a
   non-2xx body that deserialises as `T` is `Ok(T)`.
7. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/src` finds no use of
   `std::process::Command` or `tokio::process`.
8. A test calls the client against a route that never responds and asserts
   `TimedOut`.

requirements.title: `sc-transport` links axum only behind `server`

requirement_statement.text:
In `crates/sc-transport/Cargo.toml`:

4. `tokio` and `reqwest` are stated by the sc-runtime design. `serde` follows from the crate's own API: the client methods are bounded by `serde::Serialize` and `serde::de::DeserializeOwned` ([REQ-TRN-0005](requirements.md)) and the configuration type implements `serde::Deserialize` ([REQ-TRN-0001](requirements.md)). `serde_json` decodes a buffered body so `ResponseDecode` can keep `body_preview`. The list does not name `sc-observability-types`. `allowed_dependencies` does not include it. `server` still adds only `axum`.

This item is the owner of the list of third-party crates `sc-transport` may
depend on. [REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md) owns the workspace-internal
and forbidden edges and refers here for the third-party list.

statements.text: There MUST be a cargo feature named `server`.
`axum` MUST be declared `optional = true` and MUST be enabled only by the `server` feature.
With default features the direct non-dev dependencies MUST be exactly `tokio`, `reqwest`, `serde`, and `serde_json`.
With the `server` feature the direct non-dev dependencies MUST be exactly those four plus `axum`.
All listener-binding code MUST be compiled only under `#[cfg(feature = "server")]`.
The crate MUST build and pass its tests both with and without the feature.

`just test` MUST run both `cargo test -p sc-transport` and `cargo test -p sc-transport --features server` ([REQ-RUN-0004](../requirements.md)), because `cargo test --workspace` alone builds this crate only with `server` enabled.
`server` MUST NOT be in the `default` feature list.
The default build MUST NOT have `axum` anywhere in its normal dependency tree.

requirements.rationale:
The CLI of a generated project depends on this crate for its client, and a
CLI binary must link none of axum, rmcp or sqlx
([NFR-RUN-0001](../requirements.md)): linking the daemon's stack would
multiply its build time and binary size. Listener binding needs axum, so it
is opt-in. Cargo unifies features across one build, so under
`cargo build --workspace` this crate is compiled with `server` for every
member; whether such builds are exempt or the crate must be split is an
OPEN owned by [NFR-RUN-0001](../requirements.md). The criteria below are
therefore all run with `-p sc-transport`.

success_criteria.text:
1. `cargo tree -p sc-transport -e normal --prefix none` prints no line
   beginning with `axum ` (the name followed by a space).
2. `cargo tree -p sc-transport -e normal --prefix none --features server`
   prints a line beginning with `axum `.
3. `cargo test -p sc-transport` passes, run by `just test`.
4. `cargo test -p sc-transport --features server` passes, run by
   `just test`.
5. `Cargo.toml` inspection: `default` does not list `server`; `axum` has
   `optional = true`.
6. `cargo tree -p sc-transport -e normal --depth 1 --prefix none` prints,
   after the first line (the crate itself), exactly four lines, beginning
   with `reqwest `, `serde `, `serde_json `, and `tokio `.
7. The same command with `--features server` prints, after the first line,
   exactly five lines, beginning with `axum `, `reqwest `, `serde `,
   `serde_json `, and `tokio `.

requirements.title: No `hyperlocal`, custom connector or hand-written HTTP

statements.text: The crate `sc-transport` MUST make every client HTTP request, over UDS and over TCP, through `reqwest` 0.13.
For UDS it MUST use `reqwest::ClientBuilder::unix_socket(path)`.
The crate MUST NOT depend on `hyperlocal`.
It MUST NOT implement its own hyper or tower connector (for example a type implementing `tower::Service<Uri>` or hyper-util's `Connect`).
It MUST NOT write or parse HTTP messages on a raw `UnixStream` or `TcpStream`.

requirements.rationale:
Since reqwest 0.13, `ClientBuilder::unix_socket` sends HTTP over a Unix
socket with no extra crate. An earlier draft of the project assumed
`hyperlocal` or a custom connector was needed; that was factually wrong.
Standard crates used the documented way mean less code to own and review.

success_criteria.text:
1. `cargo tree -p sc-transport -e normal --prefix none` and the same command
   with `--features server` each print no line beginning with `hyperlocal `
   (the name followed by a space).
2. `crates/sc-transport/Cargo.toml` declares `reqwest` with version
   requirement `0.13`.
3. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/src` finds a call to `unix_socket(`,
   no `impl` of a hyper or tower connector trait, and no code that writes an
   HTTP request line (such as `"GET "` or `"HTTP/1.1"`) to a stream.

requirements.title: `sc-transport` depends on no other workspace crate

requirement_statement.text:
| Forbidden crate | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sc-config` | library crate of this workspace |
| `sc-command` | library crate of this workspace |
| `sc-runtime` | library crate of this workspace |
| `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | rusqlite write actor |
| `sc-cron` | SQLite-backed cron |
| `sc-observability` | the SC logging and telemetry crate |
| `sc-observability-otlp` | its OpenTelemetry export crate |
| `sc-observability-types` | its error-code crate |

The crate's boundary manifest under the repository directory
`boundaries/sc-transport/` is a TOML file. Sprint a-3 lints it as a
single-crate workspace (`sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root crates/sc-transport`).
sc-lint 0.8.0 lists a `forbidden_edges` target only when that target is a
workspace member of the lint tree, and it exits 3 for a name absent from
the workspace and from the cargo resolve
([REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md)). The root workspace includes
`sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, so `boundaries/sc-transport/sc-transport.toml` lists
`sc-transport -> sc-runtime-db-sqlite`. Other workspace-member edges from the
table above are listed when those targets are members of the lint tree.
`sc-cron` is not a member during sprint `b-1`, so it is not a
`forbidden_edges` entry yet. Crates.io names stay on the `cargo tree` check:
no line begins with `sc-config `, `sc-command `, `sc-runtime `,
`sc-runtime-db-sqlite `, `sc-cron `, `sc-observability `,
`sc-observability-types `, or `sc-observability-otlp ` (each name followed
by a space).

`allowed_dependents` is `sc-runtime`. a-5 added that name once the
four-crate workspace existed. Naming it before it was a workspace member
would make sc-lint 0.8.0 exit 3.

`allowed_dependencies` for the default build is `tokio`, `reqwest`, `serde`,
and `serde_json`. `axum` is absent from that list because the manifest has no
feature key; [NFR-TRN-0001](requirements.md) checks it with `cargo tree`.
`sc-lint-boundary` checks inter-crate edges and the public facade list only.

statements.text: The list is owned by [REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md), which states the workspace-internal and forbidden edges of all four crates; this item applies it to `sc-transport` and MUST stay identical to it.

`crates/sc-transport/Cargo.toml` MUST NOT list any of these crates under `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`, `[build-dependencies]` or any target-specific dependency table, with any feature set: (see table above)

requirements.rationale:
Each of the four crates must build and test on its own and be usable without
the other three or the template ([REQ-RUN-0002](../requirements.md)), so any
of them can be used by programs that are not sc-runtime daemons or move to
its own repository later. The three standalone crates `sc-config`,
`sc-transport` and `sc-command` have no dependency edges among them; only
`sc-runtime` knows the others ([ADR-RUN-0003](../architecture.md)).
`sc-observability` is forbidden because observability is not wrapped: a
project's `main.rs` initialises it directly and no library crate of this
workspace depends on it ([ADR-RUN-0004](../architecture.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. `cargo tree -p sc-transport -e normal --prefix none` and the same command
   with `--features server` each print no line beginning with `sc-config `,
   `sc-command `, `sc-runtime `, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite `, `sc-cron `,
   `sc-observability `, `sc-observability-types `, or
   `sc-observability-otlp ` (each name followed by a space).
2. Inspection of `crates/sc-transport/Cargo.toml` finds none of those names
   as a key in `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]`,
   `[build-dependencies]`, or a `[target.*]` dependency table.
3. A TOML manifest file exists under `boundaries/sc-transport/`. Its
   `forbidden_edges` list records the workspace-member edges
   [REQ-RUN-0005](../requirements.md) requires for `sc-transport` that are
   members of the lint tree, including `sc-transport -> sc-runtime-db-sqlite`.
   `sc-cron` is omitted until it is a workspace member, because sc-lint 0.8.0
   exits 3 for a target absent from the workspace. Its `allowed_dependents`
   list is `sc-runtime`. Its `allowed_dependencies` are `tokio`, `reqwest`,
   `serde`, and `serde_json`.
4. `sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root crates/sc-transport` exits 0. Root
   `just lint` across all four manifests stays with a-5.
5. `cargo test -p sc-transport` passes from a clean checkout.

requirements.title: `sc-transport` returns `TransportError`, never panics

requirement_statement.text:
Public functions return that enum only. `TransportCause` is the `cause` payload and the `Error::source` value. It is not a function's `Err` type.

The rule is owned by [NFR-RUN-0009](../requirements.md), which applies to every library crate of the workspace; this item applies it to `sc-transport` and adds no exception. The sc-runtime design states the rule for `sc-config` only; applying it to `sc-transport` is decided in this document. A comment does not make such a use acceptable.

No public function or method may panic because of caller input (for example
an unparseable endpoint string or a missing path) or because of environment
state (for example a missing directory, a refused connection or an
unreadable environment variable).

Every variant, its stable code, its cause payload, and its recovery are the
error-inventory table in [ADR-TRN-0001](architecture.md). The variants are
`InvalidName`, `InvalidEndpoint`, `MissingTcpPort`,
`InstanceRootUnavailable`, `DaemonNotRunning`, `ResponseDecode`, `TimedOut`,
`Request`, `Bind`, `EndpointBusy`, and `NotASocket`.

statements.text: Every public function and method of the crate `sc-transport` that can fail MUST return `Result<T, TransportError>`, where `TransportError` is one public `enum` defined in this crate.

Non-test code of `sc-transport` MUST NOT use any of the following where it is reachable from a public function: `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, panicking `[]` indexing.
Public signatures MUST NOT use opaque error types such as `anyhow::Error` or `Box<dyn std::error::Error>`.

requirements.rationale:
The crate runs inside long-lived daemons and inside CLIs driven by agents. A
panic there is an outage, or a failure no caller can parse. A typed enum lets
callers branch on the variant, and lets a generated `main.rs` turn errors
into exit codes. The same rule applies to every library crate in the
workspace: public APIs return `Result<T, E>` with one typed error enum per
crate ([ADR-RUN-0006](../architecture.md)).

success_criteria.text:
1. Inspection of the public API (`cargo doc -p sc-transport --all-features`)
   shows every fallible function returns `Result<_, TransportError>` and no
   signature mentions `anyhow` or `Box<dyn Error>`.
2. Inspection of non-test code in `crates/sc-transport/src` finds none of
   `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`,
   panicking `[]` indexing, reachable from a public function.
3. For each `TransportError` variant there is at least one test that
   triggers it and matches on that variant.
4. A test passes an unparseable endpoint value to the resolver and asserts
   `Err`; a test binds in a directory that does not exist and asserts `Err`.

decisions.title: Initial release observability shim

context.text:
The initial release required an adapter between the available observability logger and the SDK logging interface.

At the baseline, runtime/cron import a local package impersonating types 1.5.1, while explicit development generation inserts an unpublished 0.0.0 adapter around the registry 1.5.0 logger.

The problem is that the initial `0.1.1` release cannot wait for unpublished observability 1.5.1, but the baseline logging wiring depends on a 1.5.1 impersonation and an unpublished adapter.

decision.text:
The initial five-package `0.1.1` release may use actual registry observability
1.5.0 without waiting for unpublished 1.5.1. One temporary
`sc_command::observability` module owns `CanonicalLog`, `SharedCanonicalLog`,
`NoopCanonicalLog` and non-default std-only `test-util` doubles. Command remains
a leaf and gains no external dependency. Published and template observability/types registry requirements use `>=1.5.0` with no upper bound (ANC-037). Phase D retains this neutral command port and the generated private inline `LoggerAdapter`. Normal builds and tests validate compatibility with the selected versions.

Permit only cron's normal `sc-command` 0.2.0 Phase C edge (initial-release
0.1.1 retained as historical evidence) with defaults disabled and no
features. Command allowed_dependents becomes exactly runtime+cron. Runtime
uses its existing server-enabled command edge. Restore the original cron
forbidden edge and runtime-only command dependent at cleanup. All other
workspace boundaries, all five SDK normal/build/transitive full-runtime/OTLP
exclusions, and absolute sc-compose/ATM package/import exclusions remain.
The neutral event receiver is the sole exception to command's handler-trait
ban; no REST/MCP handler, extractor, router, macro or framework abstraction is
added. Canonical values/errors remain the actual published types identity.

Generated application source owns a private inline `LoggerAdapter` around one
real `Arc<v2::Logger>`; generated logger/types use `>=1.5.0` with no upper bound.
It forwards service identity and `try_log`, preserving native EventErrors,
shared handle identity, best-effort outcomes and existing lifecycle precedence.

Two explicit panic-policy changes apply. Preserve the existing infallible
Noop fallback with an invariant exception **only** for the fixed `"noop"`
ServiceName literal validated by ordinary tests against the selected types, never caller or
environment data. Generated adapter code catches unwind around **only** real
`try_log`, returning fixed value-free `EventError::Routing` code
`DAEMON.OBSERVABILITY_ADMISSION_PANIC`, cause `Logging admission panicked.`
and recovery `Restart the daemon to restore logging; the application operation
is unaffected.` No panic/event/provider payload or recursive log is included.
This does not repair poison, catch abort, suppress an application panic hook,
or protect arbitrary callbacks. `try_log` takes internal locks; prompt queue
admission is not wait-free. `CanonicalLog::emit` retains the foreign canonical
EventError signature as an explicit exception to command-owned error rules.

Delete the unpublished development facade/adapter and path/rewrite plumbing
during implementation. Replace release guards with exact bridge-profile,
all-five normal/build identity and capability checks; do not disable them.
Single multi-package verified dry run precedes publication. Actual clean
registry-generated proof follows all five publications and uses the same source
commit as the `v0.1.1` tag. Authorization, credentials, release preflight,
qualified kit/inventory and controlled-host benchmarks remain required.

Normal build/tests replace registry-availability refresh, the isolated signature/direct `Arc<Logger>` probe and the forced shim-mode-fail cleanup gate. No new cleanup work follows merely from an upstream release becoming available. Future cleanup remains separate work; the retained shim is the Phase D contract.

The local and upstream traits are nominally different. Retain a command source
path re-export only if representative current-consumer/custom-impl and ordinary
compatibility tests prove the supported selection and an explicit version strategy
requires it. No old/new SDK identity promise follows from a re-export. Choose
a coordinated breaking SDK minor if compatibility requires it; the compatibility strategy for later cleanup must not imply nominal identity from a re-export. Phase D retains the existing shim and cron edge. The bounded owned paths,
commands and proof order are in the [implementation plan](plans/phase-b/initial-release-observability-shim.md).
This documentation amendment claims no implementation, QA or publication pass.

rationale.text: This small composition-only orphan-rule bridge is justified against ADR-RUN-0002's placement rule: it wires a concrete application-owned logger to an SDK port, contains no reusable service behavior, and needs no sixth published crate.

positive: Consumers can resolve newer registry observability/types versions without an exact SDK/template pin.
negative: The retained neutral port and private inline LoggerAdapter require maintenance and ordinary compatibility tests as upstream observability versions change.

decisions.title: Framework instantiates, project wires; no command registry

context.text:
Command paths need not be hand-written; default direct conversion requires no custom transform. Consumer-side generation remains permitted follow-up work.

the framework instantiates, the project wires. The mechanism in points 1 and 2 (every operation hand-written as its own REST handler, MCP tool and CLI command, with no shared command path) was a design recommendation chosen to reach an MVP without a code generator. It is the interim form. The target is the PRD §3 command pattern: one shared write path and one shared read path, with the project supplying `Tcli`, `Tsql` and the transform. "No command registry" does not forbid that shared path.

`sc-runtime` is a `cargo-generate` template plus five published library crates
(`sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-cron`) that together give a
new project a working daemon: an Axum HTTP server, an MCP server (the `rmcp`
crate), a clap CLI and sqlx stores. Every operation of such a project must be
reachable from three surfaces: a REST route, an MCP tool and a CLI command.

An earlier plan for this scaffold used a typed command registry. A project
would register each command once, and the framework would generate the REST,
MCP and CLI adapters from the registry. That plan also called for a single
assembly point where the daemon is put together. That plan is the decision
this ADR amends: the single assembly point is kept, the command registry is
not.

A registry puts the framework between the project and Axum, rmcp and clap.
That requires wrapper types around those libraries, a macro or code generator
that this repository must maintain, and a framework opinion about what a
command is. A project could then do only what the wrappers expose.

decision.text:
1. An operation supplies request/response types and uses the shared command path.
   The interim project service function has the form
   `pub async fn create_widget(s: &Stores, input: CreateWidget) -> Result<Widget, OpError>`.
2. The REST handler (`daemon/src/routes.rs`, `#[utoipa::path]` plus an axum
   handler), the MCP tool (`daemon/src/mcp.rs`, rmcp `#[tool]`) and the CLI
   command (`cli` crate, clap derive) use each library's normal API; their source
   may be written directly or generated in a consumer follow-up. Each MUST only deserialise into the `api-types` struct
   and call the service function (the CLI reaches it over HTTP).
3. `sc_runtime::Daemon::builder()` in `crates/sc-runtime` is the single
   assembly point. It MUST do assembly only, in this order: take the config the
   project already loaded; resolve the instance root and take the
   `<instance-root>/daemon.lock` singleton; call the project's stores closure;
   merge the project's router, the OpenAPI document route, a health route and
   the MCP service if one was given; bind the listener through `sc-transport`
   and serve with graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM.
4. The workspace library crates retain the existing repo-internal macro
   policy and ban on public wrappers/re-exports of Axum, rmcp and sqlx types.
   Phase D builds no generator. This does not forbid the shared command path
   or follow-up consumer-side generation against the delivered framework.
5. The project MUST pass the builder an ordinary `utoipa_axum::OpenApiRouter`
   and, optionally, an ordinary rmcp service, each returned from a closure.
6. `Stores` is a plain struct defined by the project. `sc-runtime` MUST NOT
   inspect it; it MUST only hand the value returned by the stores closure to
   the project's routes closure and MCP closure.

`<instance-root>` is the per-application, per-user directory resolved by
sc-transport, or an explicitly supplied path; its default location is
undecided ([REQ-TRN-0002](sc-transport/requirements.md)).

The builder method names are `stores`, `routes`, `mcp`, and `run`.
`Daemon::builder` takes `&sc_transport::AppName`. v0.1 binds exactly one
listener. `TransportConfig` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and has no
`additional_endpoints` field ([REQ-RT-0001](sc-runtime/requirements.md)).
There is one `axum::Router`, served on that listener.

rationale.text: A common command path avoids repeated application behavior while retaining normal Axum, rmcp and CLI APIs.

consequences.text:
Which routes exist, which store a route uses and what data moves between
stores are project decisions in ordinary Rust. Anything Axum, rmcp or clap can
do, a project can do, using those libraries' own documentation.

The cost: nothing in these crates keeps the REST, MCP and CLI views of an
operation in step. Detecting drift between the three surfaces is left to the
sc-lint project and is not built in this repository
([ADR-RUN-0005](architecture.md)).

groups.name: A typed command registry with generated REST, MCP and CLI adapters
groups.description: A typed command registry with generated REST, MCP and CLI adapters.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected because it needs wrapper types and a generator maintained here, and limits projects to what the wrappers expose.

groups.name: A macro system that expands one annotated function into the three surfaces
groups.description: A macro system that expands one annotated function into the three surfaces.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected for the same reason: it is a proc-macro crate this repository would own, where `#[utoipa::path]`, `#[tool]` and clap derive already exist.

groups.name: A portable abstraction (a trait) over the three surfaces
groups.description: A portable abstraction (a trait) over the three surfaces.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected because it gives the framework an opinion about what an operation is and hides the libraries' real APIs from the project.

implementation.text:
Enforcement uses `arch-qa` review of each change against the six points above.
That review is the mechanism for point 4's ban on public types that wrap or
re-export an Axum, rmcp or sqlx type, because `sc-lint-boundary` has no
wrapper-type analysis; [NFR-RUN-0003](requirements.md) (standard APIs and the Phase D scope),
with its `proc-macro` and `macro_rules!` greps; the `[public] facade` list in
the `sc-runtime` boundary manifest under `boundaries/sc-runtime/`, checked by

decisions.title: Thin template; crates published and named by version

context.text:
`sc-runtime` delivers reusable code to projects in two ways: as a
`cargo-generate` template rendered once into a new project, and as library
crates the project depends on. Code rendered from a template belongs to the
project from that moment and cannot be upgraded from here. A dependency can be
upgraded with `cargo update`.

An earlier plan for this scaffold started the reusable crates as path
dependencies whose source was copied into each generated project, to be
extracted into published crates in a later phase. Copied source has no upgrade
path: every fix would have to be re-applied by hand in every project.

decision.text:
1. `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command` and `sc-runtime` MUST be separate
   crates under `crates/` from the first commit, each a member of the root
   Cargo workspace of the repository `randlee/sc-runtime`.
2. Each crate MUST be published separately to crates.io with its own version,
   README and tests, and MUST be usable without the template.
3. `template/` MUST live in the same repository as the crates, so that
   template CI can test the template against the crates at the same commit.
   `template/` MUST NOT be a member of the root Cargo workspace, because its
   files are `cargo-generate` template sources that contain placeholders and
   are not a compilable package until rendered.
4. Every `Cargo.toml` rendered into a generated project MUST name these crates
   by crates.io version requirement and MUST NOT contain a `path =` dependency
   on any of them.
5. Before the first publish, and when testing unreleased changes, a
   `[patch.crates-io]` entry or a git tag MAY stand in for the published
   version.
6. Placement rule for new code: code that should improve across all projects
   MUST go in a crate; code a project will want to edit MUST go in the
   template. Check, decided in this document: a change that adds Rust code
   under `template/` other than the example operation, the wiring of routes,
   MCP tools, CLI commands and stores, or configuration MUST state in its
   sprint document why that code cannot live in a crate.
7. `install.py` from the pinned sc-publish kit is the only owner of release
   workflows. The authored release inputs are `release/sc-publish-pin.toml`,
   `release/sc-publish-consumer-input.json`, and
   `docs/development/sc-publish.md`. `install.py` writes
   `.github/workflows/release*.yml` and the kit release scripts. Those
   outputs are generated files and MUST NOT be hand-edited.
8. Hand-authored publish workflows are forbidden, including a hand-authored
   `.github/workflows/crates-publish.yml`. A workflow of that name is
   allowed only as byte-for-byte `install.py` output.
9. The GitHub Release for tag `v0.1.0` MUST include a workspace source
   archive named `sc-runtime-{version}-source.tar.gz`. The kit produces that
   archive from the linux `release_targets` row (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`,
   `ubuntu-latest`, `tar.gz`). `release_binaries` stays empty. Phase A ships
   no release binaries.

Phase C shared-version release policy (owner correction, 2026-11-04):

The owner stated: "I expect we will release all crates every release". Every
public crate therefore participates in the same versioned release. Phase C
publishes sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron and
sc-cron-commands at 0.2.0; the internal publish=false SQLite helper stays
private. C-3 owns the coherent source/template manifest and lock migration and
canonical kit-input regeneration; c-4 owns actual authorized publication,
existing-kit qualification and registry-only consumer proof.

Historical observation, superseded as a requirement: the pinned canonical kit
b6947ab2e495398a58123c60c0b86b5421f89979 rejected a disposable mixed-version
fixture (config/transport0.1.1 versus tag0.2.0), including disabled publication
rows. That selective probe did not pass. The corrected policy uses the kit's
existing uniform-version model, so selective-publishing enhancement is not a
C1 or release prerequisite. Existing version/visibility checks and publication
authorization remain binding; no hand-written workflow bypass is allowed.

rationale.text: sc-runtime design, 2026-09-19: independent crates stated by the owner; one repository with crates.io versions is a design recommendation accepted for sprint planning. Replaces an earlier scaffold plan of path dependencies extracted later. The review check in point 6 is decided in this document. Points 7–9 are decided in sprint a-7

consequences.text:
Generated projects pick up fixes with `cargo update`. The template stays
small, which keeps the fixture matrix (one generated project per answers
fixture) cheap to run. Publishing becomes part of every release, and each
crate's public API is a semver contract from `v0.1.0`. Any crate can move to
its own repository later without an API change. The `v0.1.0` GitHub Release
carries the workspace source archive from point 9 and no release binaries.
Release workflow files stay kit output.
neutral:
OPEN: point 3's same-commit testing needs a generated project to resolve
the four crates from the checked-out `crates/` directory and not from
crates.io. Who writes the `[patch.crates-io]` entry that does this (a template
option, the driver `scripts/new_project.py`, or the CI workflow) is undecided
([REQ-RUN-0003](requirements.md)). The release run of the fixture matrix
resolves the crates from crates.io ([REQ-RUN-0702](requirements.md)), so that
run tests the published versions and not the same commit.

decisions.title: Crate dependency graph and the `server` cargo feature

context.text:
The edges in this ADR describe the code as it is and stay enforced until the code changes. Implementing PRD v2.0 changes them ([code-alignment.md](prd/code-alignment.md)).

Two properties pull against each other. Each of `sc-config`, `sc-transport`
and `sc-command` must be usable alone by programs that are not sc-runtime
daemons, and both the generated daemon and the generated CLI use
`sc-transport` and `sc-command`. Yet a CLI binary must not link Axum, rmcp or
sqlx, while the server-side halves of those two crates need Axum and rmcp.

Cargo unifies features across every package selected in one build. A cargo
feature therefore separates client and server code only when the CLI is built
as its own selection.

decision.text:
1. Workspace-internal edges and forbidden edges.
   This table mirrors [REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md), which owns it:

   | Crate | Workspace crates it depends on | Forbidden edges (`forbidden_edges`) |
   |---|---|---|
   | `sc-config` | none | `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`, `sc-observability-types`, `tokio` |
   | `sc-transport` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`, `sc-observability-types` |
   | `sc-command` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp` |
   | `sc-runtime` | MUST: `sc-transport` with its `server` cargo feature, `sc-command` with its `server` cargo feature, and `sc-observability-types` for injected canonical events. The edge `sc-runtime` -> `sc-config` is absent | `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-cron`, `sqlx` (cargo tree; not a workspace member), `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp` |
   | `sc-runtime-db-sqlite` | none | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-cron`. `sqlx` is absent and is checked with `cargo tree`, because it is not a workspace member |
   | `sc-cron` | MUST: registry `sc-observability-types`; TEMPORARY `sc-command` 0.2.0 for Phase C (initial release 0.1.1), defaults off/no features, for the contract (ADR-RUN-0017) | `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-runtime`, `sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, `sc-observability`, `sc-observability-otlp`. `sqlx` is absent and is checked with `cargo tree` |

`sc-observability-types` is allowed on `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and
`sc-cron`; command temporarily owns the contract and runtime/cron construct canonical events from the published values.
The table lists the full forbidden-edge policy. Manifest `forbidden_edges`
list only workspace-member targets in that lint tree; crates.io names use
criterion 5 `cargo tree` checks (see sprint a-1 evidence). sc-lint 0.8.0
cannot fail a crates.io edge, so direct-depth cargo-tree checks prove that
`sc-runtime` and `sc-cron` contain the types crate but not the full runtime.
`allowed_dependents` is empty for `sc-config`, `sc-runtime`,
`sc-runtime-db-sqlite`, and `sc-cron`; it is `sc-runtime` for
`sc-transport`, and temporarily `sc-runtime` plus `sc-cron` for `sc-command`
under ADR-RUN-0017. The
edge `sc-runtime` -> `sc-config` is absent. It is not an `allowed_dependents`
entry. `boundaries/sc-runtime/sc-runtime.toml` lists it under `forbidden_edges`.

2. `sc-config`, `sc-transport` and `sc-command` MUST NOT depend on one
   another, because each must be usable without the others. `sc-runtime` MUST
   be the only assembly crate depending on the other three; the sole temporary
   exception is cron -> command under ADR-RUN-0017.
3. The allowed third-party dependencies of each crate are owned by that
   crate's NFR and are not restated here:
   [NFR-CFG-0002](sc-config/requirements.md) for `sc-config`,
   [NFR-TRN-0001](sc-transport/requirements.md) for `sc-transport`,
   [NFR-CMD-0001](sc-command/requirements.md) for `sc-command`,
   [NFR-RT-0003](sc-runtime/requirements.md) for `sc-runtime`.
4. Server-side code MUST sit behind a cargo feature named `server`: in
   `sc-transport`, listener binding for `axum::serve` over UDS or TCP; in
   `sc-command`, the conversion of `Envelope<T>` into an axum response and
   into an rmcp `CallToolResult`. `axum` in `sc-transport`, and `axum` and
   `rmcp` in `sc-command`, MUST be optional dependencies enabled only by that
   feature.
5. The `server` feature MUST be off by default in both crates (decided in this
   document).
6. `sc-runtime` MUST enable `server` on both crates. A generated `cli` crate
   MUST NOT enable `server` on either crate and MUST NOT depend on
   `sc-runtime` as a normal (non-dev) dependency; the rule and its scope are
   owned by [NFR-RUN-0001](requirements.md). The full crate graph of a
   generated project is [ADR-RUN-0303](architecture.md).
7. Feature-gated code MUST be tested both with and without
   `--features server` (decided in this document). The `just test` recipe of
   [REQ-RUN-0004](requirements.md) runs `cargo test -p <crate>` with default features for
   each of the four crates, and `cargo test -p sc-transport --features server`
   and `cargo test -p sc-command --features server`.
8. The property "a CLI links none of axum, rmcp or sqlx" is defined for a CLI
   built as its own selection, `cargo build -p <project>-cli`
   ([NFR-RUN-0001](requirements.md), which owns the property and its criterion).
   v0.1 rendered that package as `cli`. Amended 2026-10-25.

The edge `sc-runtime` -> `sc-config` is absent. `sc-runtime` does not depend
on `sc-config` and does not load configuration
([NFR-RT-0002](sc-runtime/requirements.md)).

Sprint a-1 measured both selections on `examples/spike` and closed this
question. `cargo build -p cli` is the normative selection measured on that
spike. The generated package name is now `<project>-cli`
([NFR-RUN-0001](requirements.md)). Amended 2026-10-25. A workspace-wide
build is exempt from the property in point 8. Splitting `sc-transport` and
`sc-command` into client and server crates is rejected for v0.1. a-6 owns
the generated-project check `cargo tree -p cli -e normal`. a-5 does not run
that command. The measurement is the sprint a-1 evidence record.

rationale.text: sc-runtime design, 2026-09-19: independent crates stated by the owner; the `server` feature is stated in the design's repository layout. That the feature is off by default, the forbidden-edge lists, the testing rule in point 7 and the build-selection scope in point 8 are decided in this document

consequences.text:
A CLI built with `cargo build -p cli` depends on the default builds of
`sc-transport` and `sc-command` and links none of axum, rmcp or sqlx. A
workspace-wide build is exempt. The client/server crate split is rejected
for v0.1.

A shared concept cannot be shared by adding an edge between two standalone
crates. `TransportError::DaemonNotRunning` is owned by
[ADR-TRN-0003](sc-transport/architecture.md). The `OpError` wire form is
owned by [ADR-CMD-0001](sc-command/architecture.md). The Phase A decision
for the daemon-not-running code is point 5 of
[ADR-RUN-0004](architecture.md). This ADR does not restate those field
types.

`sc-lint-boundary` cannot express "axum only with `server`": its manifest
format has no cargo-feature key. Feature-conditional dependencies are checked
with `cargo tree`, and wrapper-type rules by `arch-qa` review.

groups.description: Letting `sc-command` depend on `sc-transport` so they can share the daemon-not-running error.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected because neither crate would then be usable alone.

Enforced by: the boundary manifests `boundaries/<crate>/*.toml`, checked
by `sc-lint-boundary` through `just lint`, for the inter-crate edges and

TOML with `boundary_id`, `owner_package`, `[public] facade`,
`[implementation]`, `[composition] roots`, `[dependencies]` holding

key. Feature-conditional dependencies (point 4) are enforced by `cargo tree`
checks of this form, owned by [NFR-TRN-0001](sc-transport/requirements.md) and
[NFR-CMD-0001](sc-command/requirements.md):
`cargo tree -p <crate> -e normal --prefix none` prints no line beginning with
`axum ` or `rmcp ` (the name followed by a space). For the generated `cli`
crate the check is owned by [NFR-RUN-0001](requirements.md): the same command with
`-p cli` prints no line beginning with `axum `, `rmcp ` or `sqlx `. Point 7 is
enforced by the `just test` recipe ([REQ-RUN-0004](requirements.md)).

decisions.title: `sc-observability` is initialised by the project, not wrapped

context.text:
The initial 0.1.1 release uses the planned registry 1.5.0 shim profile in
[ADR-RUN-0017](#adr-run-0017-initial-release-observability-shim). Published 1.5.1
and direct upstream Arc coercion are future cleanup requirements, not initial
publication prerequisites. Current local development packages must be removed
before initial publication. Application construction/flush/shutdown remains
owned by the generated daemon.
Every generated daemon uses the full runtime. The tempting design is to have
`sc-config` or `sc-runtime`
initialise it. That would make those crates depend on the observability
stack, so `sc-config` could no longer be used by a program that does not use
`sc-observability`, and observability would in turn be tied to how config is
loaded.

decision.text:
1. Library crates MUST NOT depend
   on `sc-observability` or on its OTel export crate `sc-observability-otlp`.
2. Library crates MUST NOT wrap `sc-observability`, re-export it, or define
   logging wrapper functions. ADR-RUN-0017 permits only the temporary neutral
   command contract and private generated-application adapter.
3. `sc-observability-types` is allowed on `sc-command`, `sc-runtime`, and
   `sc-cron`. Runtime and cron use only the command-owned
   `CanonicalLog`/`SharedCanonicalLog` port and canonical published event types; error remediation stays on `sc-command`.
   It is not allowed on `sc-config` or `sc-transport`. The logging runtime
   and OTel export stay forbidden on all library crates.
4. The generated `daemon/src/main.rs` MUST, in this order: load config with
   `sc-config`; initialise `sc-observability` directly with plain values
   taken from that config; then call `sc_runtime::Daemon::builder()`.
   Initial release uses real registry `=1.5.0` logger/types and the private
   inline adapter under ADR-RUN-0017; future upstream cleanup removes it.
5. `TransportError::DaemonNotRunning` is owned by
   [ADR-TRN-0003](sc-transport/architecture.md). It carries
   `code: &'static str` (`DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`) plus the endpoint and the
   cause. It does not carry `sc_observability_types::ErrorCode` or
   `Remediation` on the transport error. Sprint a-4's `sc-command` publishes
   a constructor from that code plus endpoint and cause into the `OpError`
   wire form (including `ErrorCode` and `suggested_action`) without adding
   a dependency from `sc-command` to `sc-transport`. a-6's generated CLI calls
   that constructor. The `OpError` wire form stays owned by
   [ADR-CMD-0001](sc-command/architecture.md). This ADR does not restate the
   rest of those field types. a-3 consumes this decision and does not add
   `sc-observability-types` to `sc-transport`.

rationale.text: sc-runtime design, 2026-09-19: stated by the owner

consequences.text:
`sc-config` has no observability dependency and can be used in any Rust
program. A project chooses its own log sinks and adds the OTel export crate
itself if it wants export.

Library lifecycle events use direct injected `LogEvent` emission; no
`tracing` bridge into `sc-observability` is assumed or added.
negative: Library lifecycle events reach `sc-observability` only through the injected `LogEvent` port; events emitted through `tracing` are not forwarded to it.

groups.description: `sc-runtime` (or `sc-config`) initialising `sc-observability` for the project.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected because it makes the library crates depend on the observability stack and removes the project's control over sinks.

groups.description: A logging facade defined inside these crates.
groups.why_rejected: Rejected because it is a wrapper this repository would maintain over a crate that is already the standard.

[REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)), checked by `sc-lint-boundary` through `just lint`;
`arch-qa` review of points 2 and 3 and of the generated `daemon/src/main.rs`

decisions.title: Lint and `just` infrastructure belong to sc-lint

context.text:
Every SC repository exposes the same base `just` commands, and Rust
repositories run a standard sc-lint setup behind them; the sc-lint repository
is the source of truth for both. An earlier scaffold plan also wanted
adapter-drift enforcement: tooling that keeps the REST, MCP and CLI views of
an operation in step. Building that tooling here, together with boundary
rules and `just` modules inside the template, would duplicate what sc-lint
owns and freeze a copy of it into every generated project, where it can never
be upgraded.

decision.text:
1. `template/` MUST NOT contain copied maintainer lint/boundary configuration,
   adapter-drift tooling, or `just` modules. The narrow fresh-install exception
   below permits configuration-derived application boundary inventory and
   the three REQ-RUN-0307 analyzer invocation declarations only. `sc-lint.toml` is the
   consumer pin. It is not a hand-written clippy, rustfmt, deny, or
   `boundaries/` policy.
2. This repository MUST NOT build surface-snapshot or adapter-drift tooling.
3. A generated project gets its `just` and lint install from sc-lint 0.8.6.
   The install command is `sc-lint init --just`. The template commits
   `template/sc-lint.toml` with `minimum_version` 0.8.6 and
   `template/.sc-lint/bootstrap.py`.
4. The public recipes are `setup`, `lint`, `test`, and `upgrade`. The
   consumer-owned recipe `db-prepare` MUST survive repeated `sc-lint init`.
   SDK custom profiles and edits to external boundary policies MUST also
   survive repeated native initialization and the public setup/upgrade flow.
   a-6 owns the generated consumer install.
5. The placeholder `Justfile` and the prototype-handoff order are retired.
   There is no step that generates prototype repositories so the sc-lint team
   can build an install from them, and no later deletion of a placeholder
   `Justfile`.
6. Decided in this document; the sc-runtime design does not state it: this
   repository's own crates MUST be linted by the standard sc-lint setup,
   including `sc-lint-boundary`, through `just lint`. `sc-lint-boundary`
   enforces inter-crate edges and each crate's public facade list only
   ([REQ-RUN-0005](requirements.md)). The single-crate command and its exit
   codes are in the sprint a-1 evidence record.

Phase C fresh-install qualification (2026-11-04):

The generated consumer needs its own default boundary policy: derive one active
record per selected application crate, with outgoing `allowed_dependencies`
and incoming `allowed_dependents` restricted to actual selected direct edges
from ADR-RUN-0303. Include api-types/service/daemon/CLI and only selected store
and MCP components; never list absent optional owners or permissions. The
policy is consumer-owned after setup; subsequent setup/upgrade and repeated
`sc-lint init --just` must preserve its edits, `db-prepare`, all three analyzer
entries, and ordinary/default/full execution. This exception supplies missing
consumer policy; it does not copy maintainer manifests, clippy/rustfmt/deny,
custom rules or `just` modules.

Released 0.8.4 inventory schema uses
`boundaries/<owner_package>/<record>.toml`: boundary_id, owner_package,
owner_crate_path and name, with public.facade, implementation, composition,
dependencies, references, testing, enforcement and status tables. Active
records use `state = "concrete_landed"`. A nonempty public facade and
`boundaries/planning.toml` with `[planning].current_sprint = "A.1"` are

decisions.title: Library errors are typed values; no public panics

context.text:
`sc-config` has a stated base requirement: every public method returns a
discriminated union (in Rust, `Result<T, ConfigError>` with a typed error
enum) and nothing panics. The same reasoning applies to all four crates: they
run inside long-lived daemons, where a panic is an outage, and inside CLIs
driven by agents, where a panic is a failure no caller can parse.

Two public signatures in `sc-command` are dictated by third-party libraries
and cannot name an sc-runtime error enum: an rmcp `#[tool]` function must
return `Result<CallToolResult, McpError>`, and axum's `IntoResponse`
conversion cannot fail.

decision.text:
The owner of the error rule and of the panic rule is
[NFR-RUN-0009](requirements.md); this ADR records the decision behind it.

1. Every fallible public function in `sc-config`, `sc-transport`, `sc-command`
   and `sc-runtime` MUST return `Result<T, E>` for the errors the crate itself
   originates, where `E` is that crate's one typed error enum: `ConfigError`
   in `sc-config`, `TransportError` in `sc-transport`, `RuntimeError` in
   `sc-runtime`. The design states this for `sc-config`; for the other crates
   it is decided in this document.
2. Recorded exception: `sc_command::IntoMcp::into_mcp` returns
   `Result<CallToolResult, McpError>`, where `McpError` is rmcp's error type,
   and the `sc-command` conversion of `Envelope<T>` into an axum response
   (`IntoResponse`) is infallible. Those signatures are dictated by rmcp and
   axum. Point 1 does not apply to them.
3. No public function in those crates may panic on caller input or on
   environment state. None of `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`,
   `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, panicking `[]` indexing may be reachable from a
   public function. There is no allowance for an exception justified by a
   code comment.
4. Public APIs MUST NOT return opaque errors such as `anyhow::Error` or
   `Box<dyn Error>`.
5. An error returned by a service function that crosses a process boundary
   MUST be an `OpError` inside the response envelope
   `{version, ok, data, error}`. `OpError` has the fields `kind`, `code`,
   `message`, `details` and `suggested_action`; `code` is a stable string such
   as `DAEMON.NOT_RUNNING`. The exact JSON keys, and whether an empty
   `details` or `suggested_action` is written as `null` or omitted, are
   defined by [REQ-CMD-0002](sc-command/requirements.md).

rationale.text: sc-runtime design, 2026-09-19: stated by the owner for `sc-config` only. Extending the rule to `sc-transport`, `sc-command` and `sc-runtime`, the one-enum-per-crate rule and the banned-construct list are decided in this document

consequences.text:
Callers can branch on error variants. The generated `daemon/src/main.rs`
returns `ExitCode` and turns config and runtime errors into exit codes and
messages. `sc-config`, `sc-transport` and `sc-runtime` each carry a small
error enum and a test per variant.
negative: The cost is maintaining each small error enum and its test per variant.
neutral:
OPEN: whether `sc-command` needs an error enum of its own, and its name if
so, is undecided. Its only fallible public function known today is
`into_mcp`, which is covered by point 2.

OPEN: whether a response the framework produces before or outside a
service function is an envelope is undecided: an axum response for an unknown
route, an axum rejection of a request body, an rmcp protocol error. The owner
of this question is [REQ-RUN-0203](requirements.md). Point 5 makes no claim about those
responses.
